title: CVD & delta panes: cumulative delta, anchors, display modes and divergence
body:
## Context
**R2 "Order-flow beta"** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6, sprints S10-S13, `v0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility on top of the R1 engine. **E23 CVD & delta panes** is the *cumulative aggression* layer of that release. The roadmap scope line (Â§6.2) reads:

> CVD computed from aggressor side with explicit session/rolling/anchored reset semantics; per-bar delta pane; CVD divergence markers; multi-symbol CVD comparison; **correct CVD reconstruction after WS reconnect** (recompute from recorded trades, never guess)

â€” **26 pts, Sprint S12**, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`), story domain **CVD** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13).

Three facts shape every ticket in this epic:

1. **CVD is exact, not estimated.** Bybit publishes the aggressor side on `publicTrade` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` â€” `TradeEvent.side` maps Bybit's `S`), so `delta = buy_volume - sell_volume` is a *measurement*, not a tick-rule inference. The only `(estimated)` surface in this epic is **divergence detection**, which is heuristic and therefore carries CMP-227 EstimatedBadge on SCR-052 (design sign-off checklist: "divergence markers drawn with a text label and the *(estimated)* chip where the detection is heuristic").
2. **One delta computation, three consumers.** US-CVD-001's NFR is explicit: "shares the delta computation used by footprint and Deep-Stats". E18 Footprint already aggregates bid/ask volume per price per bar; E20 Deep-Stats already renders per-bar delta / cumulative-delta rows. E23 must **consume** that aggregation inside M9, not fork it. A second delta implementation is an explicit anti-goal and a review-blocking defect.
3. **Reconnect must recompute, never guess.** CVD is a running sum: one lost print corrupts every subsequent value forever. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§7 provides snapshot+delta with per-topic sequence numbers and an explicit resync protocol, and Â§"Append, never merge" notes that for `trades` "**every print matters for the tape and CVD**". On any gap the series is **recomputed from the recorded tape** (QuestDB `trades` / Parquet cold tier) over the affected window and the client is re-snapshotted â€” never interpolated, carried forward, or silently re-based.

### Estimate reconciliation (roadmap-authoritative)

`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (epic register, line 123) and §6.2 size **E23 at 26 points**. That register is authoritative and this epic ticket therefore carries `estimate: 26`.

| Bucket | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering delivery in the R2 train (K01, T01-T05, S01-S05) | **27** | The number the roadmap's 26 pts is measured against — **+3.8%**, inside the ±15% planning band |
| R5-deferred story S06 (composite CVD) | 2 | Sprint `Backlog`; descope candidate 4 per roadmap §12, not part of the R2 train |
| Engineering total incl. deferred | 29 | |
| Design (D01-D06), QA (Q01-Q06), Security (X01-X02) | 33 | Discipline capacity tracked on the design/QA/security lanes; **not** rolled into the roadmap engineering points for E23 |

The epic's `estimate` field is deliberately **not** the arithmetic sum of all children: summing design, QA and security lanes into the engineering figure would double-count capacity that the roadmap tracks separately, and would make E23 appear to have blown its train window when it has not. Any change to the in-train engineering total that pushes it outside 22-30 pts must be reflected back into `30-release-roadmap.md` §3/§6.2 in the same PR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories covered:** US-CVD-001 (per-bar delta pane, *Must*), US-CVD-002 (cumulative delta with reset anchors, *Must*), US-CVD-003 (CVD display modes, *Must*), US-CVD-004 (single-bar divergence detection, *Should*), US-CVD-005 (multi-bar swing divergence detection, *Must*), US-CVD-006 (composite / normalised CVD, *Could* â€” deferred to R5 per roadmap Â§12 descoping ladder row 4).
- **Screen:** SCR-052 CVD / delta panel.
- **Components:** CMP-185 CvdPane (the epic's net-new chart primitive); reuse of CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend (M9, `server/orderflow/cvd/`):** `CvdEngine` (anchor semantics, intrabar CVD OHLC, EMA smoothing), `DivergenceDetector` (single-bar + swing), composite z-score normaliser, reconnect recompute path.
- **API:** `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` (`metric=cvd|delta|min_max_delta`, `params={"cvd":{"anchor":"..."}}`), `GET /api/v1/market/bars?include_delta=true`.
- **WS:** `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics: ["cvd","delta",...]`, `bar_type`, `param`, `throttle_ms`; `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with `include_delta` (binary `body_kind` 4 carries `i64 delta`).
- **Tables:** QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` (`cvd`, `cvd_session`, `delta_1s`), `bars_*` (`delta`, `cum_delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, `delta_pct`), `trades` (recompute source); Postgres `layout_panes.pane_kind = 'cvd'`, `chart_indicators.indicator_code IN ('cvd','delta')`.
- **Children:** design pack D01-D06 (D-S07 track), backend K01/T01-T05, frontend S01-S06, QA Q01-Q06, security X01-X02.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell aggregation and imbalance (E18), volume/delta/TPO profiles (E19), the Deep-Stats row framework (E20), DOM ladder and liquidity heatmap (E21), big-trade bubbles (E22), OI/funding/liquidation panes (E24), tape-speed / imbalance / regime / iceberg / stop-run detectors (E25), the replay clock and scrubbing (E26 â€” E23 only guarantees its engine is driven through the same pipeline).
- Alert and rule wiring for divergence events: E40 Alerts consumes the events E23 emits and E35 consumes the `cvd_divergence` metric; E23 only publishes them.
- Multi-symbol composite CVD ships in **R5** (E23-S06, sprint `Backlog`) per the descoping ladder.
- Options/GEX, spot and inverse contracts, non-Bybit venues, Android.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: CVD matches an independent offline recomputation
  Given a full recorded symbol-day in the Parquet cold tier
  When CVD, per-bar delta, min/max delta and divergence flags are recomputed offline with DuckDB
  Then every value emitted by the live pipeline matches within floating-point tolerance

Scenario: Reconnect never corrupts the running sum
  Given a client is streaming metrics.BTCUSDT and the WS drops for 45 seconds
  When the client resubscribes and a sequence gap is detected
  Then the server recomputes CVD for the gap window from the recorded tape and re-snapshots the client
  And the post-reconnect CVD equals the value an uninterrupted client would hold, exactly

Scenario: The pane holds its frame budget
  Given three CVD panes are open during a 5,000 trades/min burst
  Then the workspace sustains >= 58 fps and each pane costs <= 2 ms CPU and <= 1 ms GPU per frame

Scenario: Divergence is honest about being heuristic
  Given divergence detection is enabled
  Then every divergence marker renders with a text label and the (estimated) chip
  And the popover states the active thresholds and the known failure modes

Scenario: Partial history is never silent
  Given the recorder holds only part of the requested range
  Then the pane shows an explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
One pipeline for live and replay (roadmap exit criterion 1): `TradeEvent` -> per-bar bid/ask aggregation in M9 (shared with E18/E20) -> `CvdEngine` -> `orderflow_metrics` persistence + `metrics.{symbol}` fan-out. Per `(symbol, bar_type, param, anchor)` the engine holds the running cumulative sum, the anchor timestamp, and the intrabar path (`min_delta`/`max_delta`) required by bar invariant **BI-3** for CVD-candle mode. Anchors: `session` (from `session_anchor`, default `utc_day`), `utc_day`, `never` (anchored at the first available print and labelled with its timestamp), `manual` (client-supplied bar timestamp, clamped to the loaded range). EMA smoothing is an **overlay**, never a replacement for the raw series.

## Test plan
Epic-level gates (children carry the detail): golden-fixture parity over one recorded symbol-day, CI-blocking on drift (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4 Correctness gate); replay double-run determinism; chaos fixtures "WS disconnect + resync" and "sequence gap"; unit coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/cvd/` and >=80% on the frontend pane; contract tests against the `MetricsUpdate` and `BarsBatch` JSON Schemas in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

## Performance notes
SCR-052 budget (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 Â§Performance): the CVD series updates at a **capped 10 Hz** â€” updates coalesced from the `metrics.{symbol}` stream into one render per 100 ms frame regardless of trade rate; panel budget **<=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU per frame**; **>=58 fps with 3 CVD panels open during a 5,000 trades/min burst**; divergence detection runs incrementally on bar close, never over the whole series. Global budgets (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2): #1 frame time <=16.6 ms p95, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate), #7 frontend memory <=1.5 GB per workspace.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_cvd_engine_updates_total{symbol,anchor}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_seconds` (histogram of gap-repair duration), `cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason="ws_gap"|"anchor_change"|"backfill"}`, `cv_cvd_divergence_events_total{kind="single_bar"|"swing"}`, `cv_metrics_subscription_rejected_total{reason}`. Logs: structured `cvd.recompute` with `symbol`, `from`, `to`, `prints`, `duration_ms`. Traces: span `orderflow.cvd.recompute` as a child of the resync span. Frontend analytics (SCR-052): `cvd.interval_changed`, `cvd.mode_changed`, `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked`, `cvd.anchor_set`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.2 (Epic):
- [ ] Every child ticket Done; US-CVD-001..005 demonstrated on staging against a recorded symbol-day
- [ ] Golden-fixture parity test and replay-determinism test green in CI
- [ ] Perf budgets #1/#2/#3 and the SCR-052 pane budget measured and recorded
- [ ] A11y audit passed (axe-core clean plus a manual screen-reader pass on the table alternative)
- [ ] STRIDE threat model recorded and reviewed; security review signed off
- [ ] ADR-0017 merged; `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` updated where behaviour drifted from plan
- [ ] Storybook stories for CMP-185 (Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers) published
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO) on the built pane; QA sign-off; Owner accepts at Sprint Review

## Dependencies
- **E18 Footprint** â€” roadmap graph `E18 --> E23`; supplies the shared per-bar bid/ask aggregation in M9 that US-CVD-001's NFR mandates E23 reuse.
- **E12 Bar builders & series rendering** â€” the bar grid (`time`/`tick`/`volume`/`range`/`delta`) CVD is sampled on, plus per-bar `delta`/`min_delta`/`max_delta`.
- **E17 Market-data WS protocol & binary framing** â€” the `metrics.{symbol}` topic, sequencing and resync machinery.
- **E13 Indicators framework & v1 indicator set** â€” US-CVD-005 requires the **same confirmed-swing source as US-IND-005** (Zig Zag); E23 must not fork swing detection.
- **E16 Recorder, retention & disk budget** â€” the recorded tape the reconnect recompute and the partial-history state depend on.
- **E11 Chart engine core** â€” the pane/axis/crosshair surface CMP-185 plugs into.
- Downstream: `E23 --> E25` (detectors consume CVD); E40 Alerts and E35 rule engine consume `cvd_divergence`.

## Branch
`feat/cvd-delta-panes-<short>` per child (e.g. `feat/cvd-delta-panes-engine`). PRs <=400 LOC diff; 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner.

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
graph TD
    D01[D01 UX research] --> D02[D02 Wireframes SCR-052]
    D02 --> D03[D03 Hi-fi + CMP-185 DS entry]
    D03 --> D04[D04 Motion + a11y review]
    D03 --> D05[D05 Handoff + sign-off]
    D04 --> D05
    X01[X01 STRIDE] --> T01[T01 CvdEngine]

    T01 --> T02[T02 metrics WS + REST surface]
    T01 --> T03[T03 Reconnect recompute]
    T01 --> T04[T04 Golden-fixture parity harness]

    D05 --> S01
    S01 --> S02[S02 Reset anchors]
    S02 --> S03[S03 Display modes + smoothing]
    S01 --> S04[S04 Single-bar divergence]
    S02 --> S05[S05 Swing divergence]
    S03 --> S06[S06 Composite CVD R5]
    Q01[Q01 Test plan] --> Q02[Q02 E2E suite]
    S05 --> Q02

```

## Risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| **R7 Data accuracy** â€” one lost print silently corrupts the running sum forever | Recompute-on-gap (T03), golden-fixture parity vs DuckDB (T04), chaos test (Q06) |
| **R2 Render performance** â€” three CVD panes on top of the full order-flow scene blow the frame budget | 10 Hz coalescing cap, divergence computed incrementally on bar close only, perf scripts (Q03), spike (K01) |
| **R5 Scope** â€” composite CVD (US-CVD-006, a *Could*) eats the train | Explicitly deferred to R5 (S06, sprint `Backlog`) per roadmap Â§12 |
| **R9 Advice boundary** â€” divergence markers read as trade signals | `(estimated)` chip plus a popover stating thresholds and failure modes; inspector shows the inputs |
| **R6 Feed rot** â€” Bybit changes `publicTrade` side semantics | Adapter contract tests (E08) plus the parity harness alarming on drift |

## Agent guidance

How to pick the next ticket in this epic when multiple agents are working it in parallel:

1. **Design track first** (E23-D01, E23-D02, E23-D03, E23-D04, E23-D05, E23-D06) must clear the design-ahead rule (Done ≥2 sprints before the Story that consumes it) before any Story in its lane starts — check each Story's own `blocked_by` for the exact design ticket.
2. **Spike/engineering foundation** (E23-K01, E23-T01, E23-T02, E23-T03, E23-T04, E23-T05, E23-T06) generally has no ticket dependency on the Stories and can start immediately in parallel with design — these define the wire contract and backend engines the Stories consume.
3. **Stories** (E23-S01, E23-S02, E23-S03, E23-S04, E23-S05, E23-S06) are blocked by their named Task/Spike and design ticket per each Story's own `blocked_by` list — do not start a Story until every key in its `blocked_by` is Done.
4. **QA** (E23-Q01, E23-Q02, E23-Q03, E23-Q04, E23-Q05, E23-Q06) and **Security** (E23-X01, E23-X02) tracks run against the Stories/Tasks they test — pick these up once their named inputs are Done, not before.
5. **Parallel lanes**: two agents may safely work any two tickets that do not appear in each other's `blocked_by` chain and do not touch the same repo paths in the same PR window — check both before starting.
6. **Shared interfaces to agree first**: any change to a WS topic, REST path, DB table, or `MetricRegistry`/`MetricDescriptor` entry named across multiple children must be raised and agreed (PR to `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md`) before two agents implement against diverging assumptions.

title: UX research: how traders read cumulative delta and divergence
body:
## Context
SCR-052 is scheduled on the **D-S07** design sprint (2026-11-06 -> 2026-11-12, "CVD/derivatives panes, detector badges + (estimated) pattern", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§1.2) and consumed by engineering in E23-S01..S05. Before wireframes, the design org must establish how the personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md` actually read a CVD pane, because two of this epic's decisions are genuinely contested and must not be guessed: (a) which **reset anchor** is the sane default, and (b) how strongly a **divergence marker** may be presented before it reads as a trade signal â€” the R9 advice-boundary risk in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

This is new interaction territory for the product: US-CVD-002's manual anchor ("click a bar and choose *anchor CVD here*") is a novel affordance that does not exist on any other pane, and US-CVD-005's swing-divergence connector is the first cross-pane geometric annotation (it links price-pane swings to CVD-pane swings).

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 moderated sessions with order-flow traders (the Owner plus recruited proxies) walking through recorded BTCUSDT footage of SCR-052 behaviour.
- Findings on: default reset anchor (`session` vs `utc_day` vs `never`); mental model of "CVD candles" (US-CVD-003) vs line vs histogram and when each is preferred; whether smoothing should default on or off; how a divergence should be *labelled* so it reads as an observation, not advice; expectations for the manual-anchor gesture and its discoverability.
- A written recommendation for the **(estimated)** copy on divergence markers, feeding the epic-wide CMP-227 EstimatedBadge popover text.
- Prioritised list of states that must be designed (D02 input), including the recorder-dependent partial-history state and the stale-data state.
- Research report in the design repo, linked from SCR-052 in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
Wireframes and hi-fi comps (D02/D03), motion (D04), engineering, and any research on the derivatives pane SCR-054 (E24) or detector badges (E25) beyond sharing the `(estimated)` copy pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Defaults are evidence-backed
  When the report is reviewed
  Then the recommended default reset anchor, display mode and smoothing setting each cite at least two participant observations
  And any recommendation contradicted by a participant records the dissent and the rationale for overriding it

Scenario: The advice boundary is addressed
  Then the report proposes divergence label copy and popover copy that describes what was measured and what could make it wrong
  And the proposal is reviewed against the R9 advice-boundary risk with the Owner

Scenario: The manual anchor gesture is validated
  Given participants are asked to re-anchor CVD at a chosen bar without instruction
  Then the report records the discovery rate and the gestures attempted
  And recommends the primary affordance plus at least one keyboard-reachable alternative
```

## Technical notes / design
Use recorded footage rather than a live feed so all participants see the same market conditions; include one high-volatility burst and one thin-book period so the divergence-heuristic failure modes are visible. Capture the exact wording participants use for "CVD" and "delta" â€” the legend copy should match their vocabulary, not the codebase's.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity controls: a fixed discussion guide, two observers per session, findings tagged to participant IDs, and a synthesis review with the CDO.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Recruit at least one participant using a high-contrast or CVD-safe theme; record whether the delta sign was read from colour or from the numeric sign, which directly validates the "never colour alone" rule in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report published in the design repo and linked from SCR-052
- [ ] Recommendations reviewed by the CDO and the Owner
- [ ] The states list is handed to E23-D02 as a checklist
- [ ] The `(estimated)` copy proposal is shared with E24 and E25 for pattern consistency

## Dependencies
`E18` â€” footprint research already established how traders read per-bar bid/ask aggression; this study builds on it rather than re-asking those questions.

## Branch
`design/cvd-research` (design repo). No code PR.

title: Wireframe SCR-052 CVD / delta panel with every state
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 sketches the panel as a header of controls (`reset [session v]  smooth [EMA 9 v]  [div x]`), a CVD line, a per-bar delta histogram sharing the time axis, and a divergence text line ("price HH / CVD LH at 13:42 (flag)"). It names four states â€” **loading, streaming, reset-marker shown, recorded-history limited** â€” and the epic adds a fifth from the roadmap exit criteria: **stale data** (shaded after 2 s). This ticket turns that sketch plus the D01 findings into a complete low-fidelity specification covering every state and every control.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes for SCR-052 covering: loading; streaming (nominal); reset-marker shown (session/utc_day/manual anchors, each with its marker treatment); **recorded-history limited** (explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp, roadmap R2 exit criterion 5); stale data (>2 s without an update); empty (no recorded tape for the symbol); error (metrics subscription rejected); CVD-candles mode **disabled** because tick data is absent (US-CVD-003 NFR requires an explanation, not a silent absence).
- Layout of the two stacked series (CVD series above, per-bar delta histogram below) with the **shared time axis aligned to the price chart** (CMP-189 TimeAxis) and the CVD value axis (CMP-188 PriceAxis) â€” including how the zero line of the delta histogram is drawn.
- Control specification: reset anchor select (session / UTC day / never / manual), display mode (line / histogram / candlestick), smoothing (off / EMA n), divergence toggle with lookback, and the legend (CMP-199) contents showing the **active parameters** (required by US-CVD-005 scenario 3).
- Divergence presentation: the single-bar glyph + text label (US-CVD-004) and the multi-bar swing connector between the two swing pairs with a label (US-CVD-005), each with the CMP-227 `(estimated)` chip and popover.
- Crosshair/tooltip content (CMP-190/CMP-197): time, bar delta, CVD value, smoothed value, divergence flag.
- The **accessible table alternative** entry point in the panel header and its tabular layout (time, delta, CVD, divergence).
- Hatched treatment for bars covered by an ingestion gap (US-CVD-001 scenario 3: "affected bars are drawn hatched and excluded from derived metrics") and the provisional styling of the forming bar.
- Annotated redlines describing behaviour, not just appearance.

## Out of scope
Token-accurate colour and type (D03), motion (D04), the composite multi-symbol variant (deferred with US-CVD-006 to R5 â€” sketch one exploratory frame only, clearly marked "R5, not for build").

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is drawn
  When the wireframe set is reviewed against the SCR-052 states list plus stale-data, empty, error and candles-disabled

Scenario: Partial history is explicit
  Given the recorder holds data only from 09:12 for the requested range
  Then the frame shows a persistent banner naming 09:12 as the first available timestamp
  And the CVD series is visually truncated at that point rather than starting from zero at the range start

Scenario: Divergence never reads as advice
  Then every divergence treatment carries a text label and the (estimated) chip
  And the popover content is drawn, not deferred to engineering to invent

Scenario: The provisional bar is unmistakable
  Given the forming bar is in progress
  Then its delta bar is styled as provisional and is drawn as never flagged for divergence
```

## Technical notes / design
Respect the engine's pane model (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`: `<Pane heightRatio={0.2}><CvdSeries data={cvd} /></Pane>`) â€” the CVD pane is a sibling pane of the price pane sharing one time axis, not an overlay. Do not design anything requiring per-tick reflow of the time axis; axis alignment is owned by the host chart.

## Test plan
Design review with the CDO, an engineer from `area/order-flow` and QA (feasibility + testability). QA confirms every state has an observable trigger they can drive in a test.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes must show the focus order through the header controls, the table-alternative entry point, and how a keyboard user reaches and reads a divergence event as text. Nothing may depend on hue alone: the delta sign appears as a numeric sign and the histogram direction.

## Performance notes
Flag any treatment that would force a full-series recomputation on a settings change â€” divergence detection must run incrementally on bar close (SCR-052 performance note), so a design implying a full re-scan per keystroke is a defect at this stage, not at build time.

## Observability
Specify where the analytics events `cvd.interval_changed`, `cvd.mode_changed`, `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked` and `cvd.anchor_set` fire in the interaction flow.

- [ ] All states drawn, annotated and reviewed

## Context
The D02 wireframes become token-accurate hi-fi comps, and the epic's net-new chart primitive â€” **CMP-185 CvdPane** â€” gets a proper design-system entry rather than a one-off (DoR Â§3.1: any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off). CMP-185's contract is already sketched in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`: tier *chart-primitive*; props `data: CvdPoint[]`, `displayMode: "candlestick"|"histogram"|"line"`, `resetAnchor: "session"|"day"|"never"|"manual"`, `divergenceMarkers?: boolean`; tokens `color.text.buy/sell`; Storybook stories Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers; tests unit, visual, axe, performance.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi comps for every SCR-052 state from D02, in **light, dark, high-contrast and the CVD-safe (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia) themes** listed in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR settings, at both the compact and comfortable densities.
- Token spec: every colour, spacing, radius, stroke width and type value resolved to a named token from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. **No raw hex.** Missing values are contributed as new tokens with a name, a value, a rationale and a design-system changelog entry.
- **CMP-185 design-system entry**, specifying: the three display modes (line, histogram, candlestick) including how CVD-candle bodies/wicks are drawn from intrabar cumulative delta (`min_delta`/`max_delta`); the zero-line treatment of the delta histogram; the reset-anchor marker (a vertical rule plus a label carrying the anchor timestamp, distinct per anchor kind); the smoothing overlay drawn **on top of** the raw series, never replacing it; the provisional-bar treatment; the gap-hatched bar treatment; the single-bar divergence glyph and the multi-bar swing connector; the stale-data shading; and the legend row contents.
- Redline of the four named Storybook stories so E23-S01/S03/S05 implement them as a transcription.
- Colour-blind verification of the buy/sell (positive/negative delta) pair under all three simulations, proving distinguishability without hue.

## Out of scope
Motion timings and transitions (D04); the handoff pack (D05); any engineering work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Token-pure comps
  When the hi-fi frames are inspected
  Then every colour, spacing, radius, stroke and type value resolves to a named design token
  And any new token carries a name, a value, a rationale and a design-system changelog entry

Scenario: CMP-185 is fully specified
  Then the entry documents all three display modes, the anchor-marker treatments for session / day / never / manual, the smoothing overlay, the provisional and gap-hatched bar treatments, both divergence treatments, the stale shading and the legend contents
  And each of the four Storybook stories has a matching frame

Scenario: Colour-blind safe
  Given the positive and negative delta treatments
  When simulated under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia
  Then the two remain distinguishable without relying on hue, via the numeric sign and the bar direction

Scenario: Contrast holds in every theme
  Then all pane text meets >= 4.5:1 and all series strokes and focus rings meet >= 3:1 against the pane background in light, dark, high-contrast and CVD-safe themes
```

## Technical notes / design
Specify the **CVD-candle construction** unambiguously so engineering does not invent it: within a bar, open = cumulative delta at bar open, high = `cvd_open + max_delta`, low = `cvd_open + min_delta`, close = `cvd_open + delta` â€” this is exactly the intrabar path tracked by bar invariant BI-3 (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`). Also define the stroke-width and opacity ladder the engine should use when the pane is short (`heightRatio` as low as 0.12) so the series stays legible without re-designing.

## Test plan
Design review plus a Storybook parity checklist that E23-S01/S03/S05 must satisfy (Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers). Contrast values captured with a contrast checker and recorded in the comp annotations.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Comps must include the focus-visible treatment of every header control and the rendered table alternative. Contrast ratios are annotated per element. The `(estimated)` chip must be legible at the smallest supported font scale (100%) and at 150%.

## Performance notes
The comps must not imply per-frame text layout in the series area: labels are limited to the legend, the anchor marker and the divergence labels, all of which change at most on bar close. Anything implying per-tick glyph layout breaks the <=2 ms CPU pane budget and must be redesigned here.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi comps complete across four themes and two densities
- [ ] CMP-185 design-system entry published; new tokens contributed with changelog entries
- [ ] Contrast and colour-blind verification recorded
- [ ] CDO review passed

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the CVD / delta pane
body:
## Context
A streaming pane is a motion surface whether or not anyone designs it. `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` owns the motion vocabulary and the `prefers-reduced-motion` contract; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` Â§6.1 owns the canvas control surrogate pattern. This ticket makes both explicit for SCR-052 before engineering starts, and runs the formal a11y design review that must pass before handoff (D05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec: the forming bar's update cadence (capped at 10 Hz by the SCR-052 performance note â€” motion must not imply anything faster), the appearance of a new divergence marker on bar close, the transition when the display mode changes (US-CVD-003 requires switching to be *instant from cached values*, so the transition must be a cross-fade of at most one frame budget, never a re-animation of the series), the anchor-change transition when CVD recomputes from a new anchor, and the stale-data shading fade-in after 2 s.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for every one of the above: values still update, but transitions collapse to instant state changes.
- Accessibility review of the D03 comps against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: focus order, focus-visible treatment, the table-alternative markup contract (headers, caption, row identity), the screen-reader announcement text for each divergence event, the `(estimated)` chip's accessible name and its popover's focus management (open, trap, dismiss on Escape, return focus), and target sizes for the header controls.
- A written a11y acceptance checklist that E23-Q04 will audit against.

## Out of scope
Implementation; the handoff pack (D05); the audit itself (Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animated transition has a spec
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then each transition names its trigger, duration, easing token and its reduced-motion fallback

Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured without losing information
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every transition collapses to an instant state change
  And no information conveyed only by animation is lost

Scenario: The a11y review produces a testable checklist
  Then the checklist enumerates focus order, the table-alternative markup contract, the per-divergence announcement text and the popover focus-management rules
  And every item is phrased so QA can pass or fail it objectively
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion durations must come from existing tokens; the pane is inside the 16.6 ms frame budget shared with the whole workspace, so no transition may drive a continuous animation while the series is also streaming. The mode-switch cross-fade in particular must be bounded: US-CVD-003 scenario 2 states switching is instant from cached values, so the cross-fade is cosmetic polish that must be skippable.

## Test plan
Review session with the accessibility specialist and an `area/order-flow` engineer; the output checklist is attached to E23-Q04 as its audit basis.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

## Performance notes
No transition may exceed one frame's share of the pane's <=2 ms CPU budget; continuous background animation is prohibited on this pane.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Motion spec merged into the design-system motion documentation
- [ ] Reduced-motion behaviour specified for every transition
- [ ] A11y review completed and the checklist handed to E23-Q04
- [ ] Accessibility specialist sign-off

body:
## Context
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, a UI story is not Done until design has verified the built result against the handoff pack. SCR-052 carries its own **design sign-off acceptance checklist** in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, and this ticket executes it against the running application on staging:

> [ ] CVD line + per-bar delta histogram drawn together with a shared time axis aligned to the chart [ ] session / anchored / rolling modes drawn [ ] divergence markers drawn with a text label and the *(estimated)* chip where the detection is heuristic [ ] recorder-dependent empty state [ ] stale-data shading after 2 s [ ] accessible table alternative reachable from the panel header

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side comparison of the built pane against the D03 comps for every state, in light, dark, high-contrast and CVD-safe themes at both densities.
- Execution of the SCR-052 sign-off checklist above, item by item, with evidence (screenshots) per item.
- Verification of the motion spec from D04, including `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Token audit: confirm no raw hex or off-token spacing reached the implementation (inspect the built CSS/engine uniforms against the token set).
- Defect tickets filed for every deviation, classified as blocker / major / minor, with the blocking ones raised before the R2 PRR.
- A written design sign-off (or an explicit refusal with the blocking list).

## Out of scope
Functional QA (E23-Q02), the a11y audit (E23-Q04), performance measurement (E23-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The SCR-052 checklist is fully executed
  Then each of the six checklist items has a pass or fail verdict with attached evidence
  And every fail has a filed defect ticket with a severity

Scenario: No token drift reached production
  When the built pane's colours and spacing are inspected
  Then every value matches a named design token
  And any raw value is filed as a defect

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional on blockers
  Given at least one blocker-severity deviation exists
  Then design sign-off is withheld and the epic cannot be marked Done
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the sweep against a recorded symbol-day replayed through the live pipeline, so all states (including gap-hatched bars, partial history and stale data) are reproducible on demand rather than waited for.

## Test plan
Manual comparison sweep with screenshot evidence; theme and density matrix fully enumerated (4 themes x 2 densities x all SCR-052 states).

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
The sweep verifies the *visual* a11y properties (contrast, focus-visible, non-colour encoding of the delta sign); the behavioural audit is E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
If a visual treatment is found to have been simplified by engineering to hold the frame budget, the deviation is recorded as a **design decision to revisit**, not automatically as a defect â€” the budget wins, and the comps are updated.

## Observability

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states compared across themes and densities with evidence

title: Spike: intrabar CVD OHLC cost and 1M-print recompute inside 2 s
body:
## Context
Two NFRs in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13 are quantitative and neither is obviously achievable without measurement:

- **US-CVD-002 NFR:** "recomputation from stored prints for **1M prints <=2 s**" â€” this is the reconnect-repair and anchor-change path (E23-T03).
- **US-CVD-003 NFR:** "intrabar CVD OHLC **requires tick data**; without it the mode is disabled with an explanation" â€” so we must establish exactly when tick data is and is not available, and what the per-bar cost of tracking the intrabar path is.

A spike is warranted because the answer determines whether the recompute runs in the request path (simple) or must be pushed to a background job with a "repairing" UI state (a materially different design for E23-T03 and E23-S02), and because the choice of query engine (QuestDB hot tier vs DuckDB over Parquet, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md`) for the recompute is not yet settled for this query shape.

## Scope / Deliverables

- A measurement of the marginal cost of tracking the **intrabar path** (`min_delta`/`max_delta`, bar invariant BI-3) versus endpoint-only delta, per 100k prints, in the bar-builder hot loop.
- A written determination of when CVD-candle mode (US-CVD-003) must be **disabled**: the precise condition in terms of recorded stream availability (`recorded_symbols.streams` contains `trades`) and the requested range versus the recorder's first available timestamp.
- A recommendation for E23-T03: in-request recompute vs background repair, with the crossover print count.
- Whether `orderflow_metrics.cvd` / `cvd_session` (1 s cadence, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Â§4.11) can serve as a **checkpoint** to bound recompute work â€” i.e. recompute only from the last persisted 1 s sample rather than from the anchor â€” and what error, if any, that introduces.
- Findings written up as a spike report and folded into ADR-0017 (E23-T05).

## Out of scope
Building the production engine (E23-T01), the repair path (E23-T03), or any UI.

```gherkin

  And quantifies any resulting deviation against a full recompute over the same window, or proves it is exact

Scenario: A negative result is still a result
  Given no approach achieves p95 <= 2 s for 1M prints
  Then the report recommends the background-repair design with a concrete UI contract for the repairing state
  And E23-T03 and E23-S02 are updated before Sprint 12 planning
```

## Technical notes / design
Use a real recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day from the E16 recorder as the fixture (a synthetic uniform tape understates the cost â€” real prints cluster). Run on the reference hardware of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§3.1 so numbers are comparable with other budgets. Measure cold and warm cache separately; the reconnect path will usually be warm for the hot tier and cold for Parquet.

Delta per print is `+qty` when `side == "Buy"` (taker bought) and `-qty` when `side == "Sell"`, per the `TradeEvent` mapping in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`; the intrabar path requires folding prints in timestamp order and tracking the running min and max of the cumulative intrabar sum, which is why it cannot be expressed as a pure SQL aggregate without a window function â€” quantify that difference explicitly.

The benchmark harness itself is the deliverable artifact and is checked into `bench/orderflow/cvd_recompute_bench.py` so E23-Q03 can reuse it. ## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

Target: US-CVD-002's 1M prints <= 2 s. Secondary constraint: the intrabar-path tracking must not push the bar builder past the per-symbol CPU budget (#11, <=0.5 vCPU sustained per actively-recorded symbol, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2).

The benchmark emits timings in the same metric names the production path will use (`cv_cvd_recompute_seconds`) so the dashboards are pre-validated.

title: Implement CvdEngine in M9: anchors, intrabar path and EMA smoothing
body:
## Context
The backend heart of the epic. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` places CVD inside **M9** (`server/orderflow/` â€” "footprint, profile, **cvd**, imbalance, heatmap, tape"), and US-CVD-001's NFR requires it to **share the delta computation used by footprint and Deep-Stats**. E18 has already built the per-bar bid/ask aggregation; this ticket adds the cumulative layer on top of it and persists the result to `orderflow_metrics`.

The engine is the single source of truth: the pane (E23-S01..S05), the alerts (E40), the rule-engine metric `cvd_divergence` (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Â§metric vocabulary) and the detectors (E25, roadmap graph `E23 --> E25`) all read its output. There is exactly one implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/cvd/engine.py` â€” `CvdEngine`, keyed by `(symbol, bar_type, param, anchor_spec)`, consuming the per-bar aggregate emitted by E18's aggregation stage (not raw prints â€” the fold over prints already happens there).
- **Anchor semantics** (US-CVD-002): `session` (reset at `session_anchor`, default `utc_day`), `utc_day`, `never` (anchor at the first available print; the engine reports that timestamp so the UI can label the start point), `manual` (a client-supplied bar timestamp, clamped to the loaded range). A reset emits an explicit `CvdResetMarker` event carrying the anchor timestamp and kind so the UI can mark it (US-CVD-002 scenario 1: "CVD resets there and the reset is marked").
- **Intrabar path** for CVD-candle mode (US-CVD-003): per bar, `cvd_open`, `cvd_high = cvd_open + max_delta`, `cvd_low = cvd_open + min_delta`, `cvd_close = cvd_open + delta`, taken from the bar's `min_delta`/`max_delta` (bar invariant **BI-3**, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`), plus an availability flag derived from the E23-K01 precondition so the API can report the mode as unavailable with a reason rather than returning wrong candles.
- **EMA smoothing** as an additional series, never a replacement (US-CVD-003 scenario 3: "a smoothed overlay renders and the raw series remains visible"). Period configurable, default 9.
- **Gap handling** (US-CVD-001 scenario 3): bars covered by a recorded ingestion gap are flagged `gapped=true` and **excluded from derived metrics**; the flag travels with the bar to the client.
- **Provisional bar**: the forming bar's CVD value is emitted with `confirm=false` so the UI can style it as provisional and so divergence detection (E23-T01's sibling detector, built in E23-S04/S05) never fires on it.
- Persistence: write `cvd`, `cvd_session` and `delta_1s` to QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` at the 1 s cadence that table specifies (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Â§4.11, `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)`), so the series is cheaply scrubbable and can act as a recompute checkpoint if E23-K01 approved that.
- A pure, side-effect-free `recompute(prints_or_bars, anchor) -> series` function, so the same code serves live, replay, backfill and the parity harness â€” one code path, per roadmap R2 exit criterion 1.

## Out of scope
The WS/REST surface (E23-T02), the reconnect repair orchestration (E23-T03), divergence detection (E23-S04/S05 own the detector), composite/normalised CVD (E23-S06, R5), any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Delta is not recomputed independently
  When the CvdEngine source is reviewed
  Then it consumes the per-bar bid/ask aggregate produced by the footprint aggregation stage
  And contains no second fold over raw prints for the purpose of computing delta

Scenario: Session anchor resets and marks
  Given the anchor is session with session_anchor utc_day
  When the series crosses 00:00 UTC
  Then the cumulative value resets to zero at that boundary
  And a CvdResetMarker carrying the anchor kind and timestamp is emitted exactly once

Scenario: Never-reset labels its start
  Given the anchor is never
  Then the series accumulates across the whole loaded range
  And the engine reports the timestamp of the first available print as the series start

Scenario: Manual anchor recomputes forward only
  Given an existing series anchored at session
  When a manual anchor is set at bar T
  Then the series from T forward is recomputed from that anchor
  And values before T are unchanged in the persisted 1 s samples

Scenario: Intrabar OHLC obeys the bar invariant
  Given a bar with delta 12, min_delta -3 and max_delta 20 and cvd_open 100
  Then the CVD candle is open 100, low 97, high 120, close 112
  And low <= open <= high and low <= close <= high always hold

Scenario: Candles are refused, not faked, without tick data
  Given the requested range predates the recorder's first available print for the symbol
  When CVD-candle mode is requested
  Then the engine reports the mode unavailable with a machine-readable reason
  And emits no candle values for that range

Scenario: Gapped bars are excluded
  Given an ingestion gap covers bars 40 to 44
  Then those bars are flagged gapped
  And they are excluded from the derived smoothing and from divergence inputs

Scenario: Smoothing never hides the raw series
  Given EMA smoothing of period 9 is enabled
  Then both the raw and the smoothed series are emitted as separate series
```

## Technical notes / design
State per key: `cum: Decimal`, `anchor_ts: int`, `anchor_kind: Literal["session","utc_day","never","manual"]`, `last_bar_ts: int`. Use the same decimal/quantity type as `TradeEvent.qty` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`) â€” no float accumulation in the running sum, because a running sum over millions of prints is exactly where float error compounds and roadmap exit criterion 6 demands parity with an offline DuckDB recomputation.

An anchor change is **not** an incremental operation: it invalidates the cumulative state and triggers `recompute()` over the affected window with `reason="anchor_change"`. Reuse the recompute entry point E23-T03 wires to the resync path so there is one repair implementation.

Config keys: `orderflow.cvd.default_anchor` (default `session`), `orderflow.cvd.session_anchor` (default `utc_day`), `orderflow.cvd.smoothing_default_period` (default `9`), `orderflow.cvd.persist_cadence_ms` (default `1000`), `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints` (clamp, default `5_000_000`). Error codes: `CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE`, `CVD_ANCHOR_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `CVD_RECOMPUTE_TOO_LARGE`.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** delta sign mapping from `TradeEvent.side`; session reset at the UTC boundary including a bar that straddles it; `utc_day` vs `session` equivalence when `session_anchor=utc_day`; never-reset start labelling; manual anchor inside, at and outside the loaded range; intrabar OHLC from (delta, min_delta, max_delta) including the degenerate `min == max == delta` case; EMA warm-up behaviour for the first n-1 bars; gapped-bar exclusion; provisional-bar `confirm=false`; decimal precision over a 1M-print fold.

title: Expose CVD and delta over metrics.{symbol} WS and /market/metrics
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Â§0.4 states the design constraint plainly: "**Derived order-flow series share one topic.** CVD, tape speed, imbalance, regime and the estimated detectors are all `metrics.{symbol}`, selected by the `metrics` option... They are one engine output family and one subscription, not five." SCR-052's data line confirms: "WS `metrics.{symbol}`, bootstrap `GET /api/v1/market/metrics?symbol&interval&from&to`".

E17 has already built the topic machinery, sequencing and resync. This ticket wires the `CvdEngine` output into that existing surface â€” it adds metric codes and options, it does not add a topic.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** E17 already owns the `metrics.{symbol}` topic machinery, sequencing, resync and the `MetricsUpdate` schema; this ticket adds metric codes, options and the REST bootstrap branch to an existing surface, so it is sized as an extension, not a new transport.

## Scope / Deliverables
- WS: support `metrics: ["cvd", "delta", "min_max_delta"]` on `metrics.{symbol}` with the documented options `bar_type`, `param`, `throttle_ms` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§topic table), plus per-metric params via the existing params mechanism â€” specifically `{"cvd": {"anchor": "session"|"utc_day"|"never"|"manual", "session_anchor": "utc_day", "manual_anchor_ts": <ms>, "smoothing": {"kind":"ema","period":9}}}`.
- Emit frames conforming to the existing `MetricsUpdate` schema (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14), each series carrying `metric`, `estimated` (**false** for `cvd` and `delta` â€” they are measured, not inferred), `unit` (`base_volume`), `t_ms` and `v`; the subscribe ack echoes `effective` options exactly as Â§5 requires.
- Carry the epic's extra per-bar attributes alongside: `confirm` (provisional forming bar), `gapped`, and the `CvdResetMarker` events, so the pane can render provisional styling, hatching and reset markers without a second request.
- REST bootstrap: `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` support for `metric=cvd|delta|min_max_delta` with the `params` JSON override documented in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`{"cvd":{"anchor":"utc_day"}}`), returning each series with its **parameter echo** so charts are reproducible, and returning the series start timestamp for `anchor=never`.
- REST: ensure `GET /api/v1/market/bars?include_delta=true` returns `delta`, `cvd`, `min_delta`, `max_delta` per bar as the OpenAPI examples already show, sourced from the same engine.
- **Partial-history reporting**: when the requested `from` predates the recorder's first available print, the response reports the first available timestamp in a machine-readable field rather than silently truncating â€” this is what the UI renders for roadmap R2 exit criterion 5.
- **Candles availability**: report `CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE` with a reason when the intrabar precondition is unmet, so US-CVD-003's "disabled with an explanation" is data-driven.
- Server-side clamping per the threat model: `maxItems: 12` on `metric` (already in the OpenAPI schema), a maximum range per request, a maximum `metrics` count and a minimum `throttle_ms` per session, and validation of `manual_anchor_ts` against the requested range.
- Contract tests against the `MetricsUpdate` and `BarsBatch` JSON Schemas and against the OpenAPI document; `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` updated if anything drifted.

## Out of scope
A new topic or endpoint of any kind; the reconnect repair logic (E23-T03); the frontend subscription client (E23-S01); composite multi-symbol series (E23-S06, R5).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One subscription carries the family
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["cvd","delta"]
  Then a single subscription is created
  And the ack echoes the effective throttle_ms, bar_type, param and per-metric params

Scenario: CVD is not marked estimated
  When a cvd or delta series frame is decoded
  Then its estimated field is false
  And the unit is base_volume

Scenario: REST and WS agree
  Given a REST bootstrap for a closed range and a WS attach for the same range
  Then the overlapping values are identical to the last emitted decimal

Scenario: Partial history is reported, not hidden
  Given the recorder's first print for the symbol is at 09:12 and from is 08:00
  Then the response reports 09:12 as the first available timestamp
  And contains no values before it

Scenario: Candles unavailability is explicit
  Given the intrabar precondition is unmet for the requested range
  When min_max_delta is requested
  Then the response carries the reason code CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE
  And no fabricated high or low values are returned

Scenario: A hostile subscription is refused
  Given a client requests 12 metrics across 40 symbols with throttle_ms 1
  Then the subscription is refused or clamped to the configured session limits
  And the rejection is counted and logged with its reason

Scenario: An out-of-range manual anchor is rejected
  Given manual_anchor_ts lies outside the requested range
  Then the request fails with CVD_ANCHOR_OUT_OF_RANGE and a 422 response
```

## Technical notes / design
Do not introduce a binary `body_kind` for metrics: the Â§3.4 binary layouts cover book, trades, bars, footprint and heatmap; metrics are low-cardinality and scalar, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14 shows them travelling as JSON (`"e":"j"`) inside the MessagePack envelope. The 10 Hz UI cap (SCR-052) is enforced client-side by coalescing; the server's `throttle_ms` default for `metrics.{symbol}` stays as documented (250 ms) â€” do not lower it to chase perceived smoothness, because that multiplies fan-out cost (budget #6, <=20 ms p95 backend-internal add-on).

Config keys: `ws.metrics.max_metrics_per_sub` (12), `ws.metrics.min_throttle_ms` (100), `ws.metrics.max_subs_per_session`, `api.metrics.max_range_days`.

## Test plan
- **Contract:** every emitted frame validated against `MetricsUpdate`; every REST response against the OpenAPI schema; the subscribe-ack `effective` echo asserted field by field.
- **Unit:** params parsing and validation (anchor kinds, malformed JSON, oversize `params` string >2048 chars, out-of-range `manual_anchor_ts`); clamping logic; partial-history field computation.
- **Integration:** REST-then-WS handoff with no duplicated or missing points at the seam; reconnect with `from_seq` attach.
- **Load:** included in E23-Q03's k6 script â€” 10 symbols x 3 metrics, sustained, asserting budget #6.
- **Coverage:** >=85% on the changed modules.

Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Backend fan-out add-on must stay within budget #6 (<=20 ms p95 from engine update to outbound frame). WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms is a **hard R2 exit gate** (budget #3) and this path is on it. Serialisation must not allocate per point in the hot path.

title: Recompute CVD from the recorded tape on WS gap or reconnect
body:
## Context
This is the ticket the roadmap singled out for this epic: "**correct CVD reconstruction after WS reconnect** (recompute from recorded trades, never guess)" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.2). It matters more here than anywhere else in R2 because CVD is a *running sum*: a footprint cell that misses a print is wrong for one bar, but a CVD series that misses a print is wrong **forever after**, silently, and by an amount no user can detect by looking.

The protocol already gives us the detection primitive: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§7 defines per-topic sequence numbers and an explicit resync protocol, and notes that for `trades` the merge rule is "**Append, never merge** ... Every print matters for the tape and CVD." Guarantee G3 states "Correctness under loss is deterministic, not best-effort."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Gap detection on the ingestion side: when the trade stream's sequence is broken, or the adapter reconnects after a disconnect, mark the affected `(symbol, window)` as **suspect** and trigger a repair rather than continuing to accumulate.
- Repair path: call `CvdEngine.recompute()` over the suspect window sourced from the **recorded tape** â€” QuestDB `trades` for the hot window, the Parquet cold tier via DuckDB beyond retention â€” using the approach E23-K01 recommended (including the `orderflow_metrics` 1 s checkpoint optimisation if it was proven exact).
- Correct the persisted `orderflow_metrics` rows for the window (the table is `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)`, so repair is an upsert, not a delete-and-insert) and re-derive every downstream cumulative value.
- Re-snapshot subscribed clients: after repair, push a fresh `metrics.{symbol}` snapshot rather than a delta, so no client holds a value derived from the corrupt prefix. The resync follows the existing Â§7 protocol; no bespoke mechanism.
- **Recorder-gap case:** if the recorded tape itself has a hole (the recorder was down, or the symbol was not recorded), the window is marked `gapped` and the affected bars are excluded from derived metrics (US-CVD-001 scenario 3) and surfaced to the UI â€” CVD is **not** interpolated across the hole, and the series start is re-labelled if the hole touches the anchor.
- A `repairing` state exposed to the client so the pane can show it, per the E23-K01 recommendation if repair is asynchronous.
- Clamping: repairs are bounded by `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints`; a window exceeding it degrades to marking the range `gapped` rather than running an unbounded scan (this is the DoS control from the threat model).

## Out of scope
Book resync (E21/E08 own `BookDesyncEvent`), replay-specific reconstruction (E26), the pane's rendering of the repairing/gapped states (E23-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reconnect produces the exact uninterrupted value
  Given a client streaming metrics.BTCUSDT with anchor session
  And the upstream trade stream is severed for 45 seconds during which 8,000 prints occur
  When the stream reconnects and the gap is detected
  Then CVD is recomputed for the gap window from the recorded tape
  And the post-repair cumulative value equals, to the last decimal, the value computed by an uninterrupted run over the same recorded prints

Scenario: The corrupt prefix never reaches a client
  When a repair completes
  Then subscribed clients receive a fresh snapshot rather than a delta
  And no client retains a value derived from the pre-repair accumulation

Scenario: A hole in the recording is admitted, not smoothed
  Given the recorder was not running for part of the gap window
  Then the affected bars are flagged gapped and excluded from derived metrics
  And no interpolated CVD value is emitted for them

Scenario: Repair is bounded
  Given a gap window containing more prints than orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints
  Then the repair is refused, the window is flagged gapped, and the refusal is logged and counted
  And the service does not run an unbounded scan

Scenario: Repeated flapping does not stampede
  Given the upstream stream disconnects and reconnects five times in one minute
  Then repairs for overlapping windows are coalesced into one
  And the repair count metric reflects the coalescing
```

## Technical notes / design
Repair is idempotent by construction: `recompute(window)` is pure and the persistence is an upsert on `(ts, symbol)`. Coalesce overlapping repair requests through a per-symbol repair queue with a single in-flight repair; a new gap arriving during a repair extends the window rather than starting a second job.

Ordering guarantee: prints are folded in recorded timestamp order with a deterministic tie-break (by the exchange trade id) so that two repairs over the same window always produce the same result â€” this is what makes the replay double-run determinism test (roadmap Â§6.4) pass for CVD.

Error codes: `CVD_RECOMPUTE_TOO_LARGE`, `CVD_RECORDING_GAP`. Config: `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints`, `orderflow.cvd.repair_coalesce_ms` (default 2000).

## Test plan
- **Unit:** gap-window computation from sequence numbers; repair coalescing (overlapping, adjacent, disjoint windows); the bounded-refusal path; tie-break ordering determinism.
- **Integration:** against the recorded fixture "WS disconnect + resync" and "sequence gap" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4 Integration gate). The key assertion is the equality of post-repair CVD with an uninterrupted run over the same fixture.
- **Chaos:** owned by E23-Q06 â€” repeated disconnects, a disconnect straddling a session anchor, a disconnect while the recorder is also down, and a disconnect during an in-flight repair.
- **Property:** for any partition of a print sequence into "live" and "repaired" segments, the final cumulative value is invariant.
- **Coverage:** >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.
Additionally: an attacker-controlled or malfunctioning upstream that flaps continuously must not be able to drive unbounded recompute work â€” the coalescing queue and the print clamp are the specific controls, and E23-X02 tests them as an abuse case.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Repair must meet US-CVD-002's NFR envelope (1M prints <= 2 s) as validated in E23-K01; repair runs off the ingestion hot path so it must not stall live accumulation for other symbols. During repair, the per-symbol CPU budget (#11) may be exceeded transiently; sustained exceedance is a defect.

## Observability
`cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason="ws_gap"|"reconnect"|"anchor_change"|"backfill"}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_seconds`, `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_repair_queue_depth{symbol}`, `cv_cvd_gapped_bars_total{symbol}`. Structured log `cvd.recompute` with `symbol`, `from`, `to`, `prints`, `duration_ms`, `source="questdb"|"parquet"`. Trace span `orderflow.cvd.recompute` as a child of the resync span. An alert fires if `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total` increases, because a refusal means a user is looking at a knowingly incomplete series.

## Context

E18 and E19 are building the footprint and profile halves of this harness; this ticket adds the CVD and per-bar-delta assertions to the same harness rather than creating a parallel one.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** E18/E19 build the golden-fixture parity harness itself (runner, fixture format, CI gate); this ticket adds CVD and per-bar-delta assertions plus the DuckDB recompute query to that existing harness.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An **independent** reference implementation of CVD in SQL over the Parquet cold tier (DuckDB), deliberately written from `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13 and `24-internal-schemas.md` rather than by reading the engine code â€” the point is independence, and a transliteration of the engine proves nothing.
- Version-controlled expected outputs for one recorded symbol-day: per-bar `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, cumulative `cvd` under each anchor kind (`session`, `utc_day`, `never`), CVD-candle OHLC, and the EMA-9 smoothed series.
- A comparison runner asserting engine output equals the reference within an explicit tolerance, with a first-divergence report (bar timestamp, expected, actual, delta) so failures are debuggable rather than merely red.
- **Replay determinism** assertion: replaying the same recorded window twice produces byte-identical CVD output (roadmap Â§6.4 Determinism gate) â€” including a run that injects a mid-window disconnect so the repair path (E23-T03) is exercised inside the determinism check.
- CI wiring: runs on every PR touching `server/orderflow/`, blocking on drift; fixture stored per the testing strategy's fixture conventions (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).
- Documented procedure for regenerating the golden outputs, requiring an explicit human justification in the PR description â€” regeneration must be a deliberate act, never a convenient one.

## Out of scope
The footprint and profile assertions (E18/E19 own them in the same harness), performance benchmarking (E23-Q03), UI verification (E23-Q02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity over a full symbol-day
  Given one recorded symbol-day in the Parquet tier
  When the engine output and the DuckDB reference are compared for every bar
  Then all delta, min_delta, max_delta, cvd and CVD-candle values match within the documented tolerance
  And the tolerance is stated numerically, not described as approximately equal

Scenario: Drift fails the build
  Given a change that shifts one bar's cumulative value by one tick of quantity
  When CI runs
  Then the job fails and the report names the first diverging bar with expected and actual values

Scenario: Determinism across runs
  When the same recorded window is replayed twice
  Then the two CVD output streams are byte-identical

Scenario: Determinism across a repair
  Given a replay run in which the stream is severed mid-window and repaired
  Then its CVD output is byte-identical to the uninterrupted replay of the same window

Scenario: Regeneration is deliberate
  Given a developer regenerates the golden outputs
  Then the PR fails review unless it contains a written justification for each changed expected value
```

## Technical notes / design
Tolerance: the engine accumulates in decimal, the DuckDB reference in `DECIMAL` as well, so the expected comparison is **exact** for delta and cumulative values; only the EMA series needs a float tolerance, and it should be stated as a relative epsilon (e.g. `1e-12`). Prefer failing on exactness where exactness is achievable â€” an unnecessarily loose tolerance is how silent drift ships.

Fixture selection matters: choose a symbol-day containing a session boundary, a volatility burst, and at least one recorded ingestion gap, so the anchor reset, the intrabar path and the gapped-bar exclusion are all covered by the single golden fixture.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test infrastructure; its own tests are meta-tests: the harness must (a) detect a deliberately seeded one-unit drift, (b) detect a reordering of prints, (c) pass on the unmodified engine. All three are asserted in CI so the harness cannot silently stop checking.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.
The fixture contains public market data only; no key material or account data may enter the fixture set.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
The harness must complete within the CI time budget for a per-PR job; if a full symbol-day is too slow, run a fixed representative window per PR and the full day nightly â€” but the full-day run must exist and must block the release, not merely warn.

Publishes the parity result and the first-divergence report as a CI artifact; the nightly full-day run posts its result to the team channel on failure.

title: ADR-0017: CVD anchor semantics, reconnect recompute and divergence determinism
body:
## Context
Three decisions made in this epic are durable, cross-cutting and will be questioned later by anyone reading the code â€” exactly what `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` says an ADR is for. They are not obvious, and rediscovering them from the implementation would be expensive:

1. **Anchor semantics.** Why `session` is the default, why `never` labels its start with a timestamp rather than starting at zero, and why a manual anchor triggers a full recompute forward instead of an offset adjustment.
2. **Recompute-on-gap over interpolation.** Why a running sum is repaired from the recorded tape rather than carried forward, and what happens when the recording itself has a hole (flag as gapped, exclude from derived metrics, never interpolate).
3. **Divergence determinism.** Why divergence detection is driven by the **confirmed-swing source shared with US-IND-005** and never fires on provisional swings or the forming bar â€” the no-repaint guarantee â€” and why divergence is nonetheless labelled `(estimated)` while CVD itself is not.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0017-cvd-anchors-recompute-and-divergence.md` in the standard ADR format (Context / Decision / Status / Consequences / Alternatives considered).
- Alternatives considered, each with the reason for rejection: carrying the last value forward across a gap; re-basing CVD to zero on reconnect; computing CVD client-side from the trade stream; running divergence detection over the whole series on every settings change; treating `never` as "since the first loaded bar" rather than "since the first available print".
- Record the E23-K01 findings (recompute cost and the candles precondition) as the empirical basis.
- Updates to the plan docs where the implementation clarified or changed them: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-185, `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/market/metrics` cvd params), `23-ws-protocol.md` (`metrics.{symbol}` cvd options), `21-database-schema.md` Â§4.11 if the persisted columns changed.
- A short "CVD correctness" section in the operator runbook: what a repair refusal means, what a gapped bar means, and what to check first when a user reports "the CVD looks wrong".

## Out of scope
New decisions â€” an ADR records what was decided and why, it does not decide. Any behaviour change belongs in its own ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR is complete and accepted
  Then ADR-0017 exists with Context, Decision, Status Accepted, Consequences and Alternatives considered
  And it is approved by the architect and an area/order-flow code-owner

Scenario: Every rejected alternative is explained
  Then each of the five listed alternatives has a stated reason for rejection
  And the reasons cite either a measurement from E23-K01 or a documented requirement

  Given the built behaviour of E23
```
