title: Render the per-bar delta pane (SCR-052, CMP-185) with live and gapped bars
body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-001 â€” Per-bar delta pane (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want a per-bar delta histogram, so that I see net aggression bar by bar." This is the foundation story of the epic â€” it creates the pane, the subscription, the axes wiring and the base component, which S02-S05 then extend.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` models the CVD pane as a sibling pane of the price pane (`Pane[0..n]` â€” "price pane, CVD pane, OI pane, volume pane") with the shape `<Pane heightRatio={0.2}><CvdSeries data={cvd} /></Pane>`, sharing the host chart's time axis. The pane is **not** an overlay and does not own time-axis panning.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-052** CVD / delta panel scaffold: the panel chrome, header controls area, legend (CMP-199) and the two stacked series regions, built from the E23-D05 handoff pack.
- **CMP-185 CvdPane** component with the catalogued props (`data: CvdPoint[]`, `displayMode`, `resetAnchor`, `divergenceMarkers?`) â€” this story implements the `histogram` per-bar delta rendering and the base series plumbing; `line` and `candlestick` land in S03.
- Signed delta histogram with a **zero line** and **sign labels** (US-CVD-001 scenario 1), rendered against CMP-188 PriceAxis with CMP-189 TimeAxis shared with the price chart, and CMP-190 Crosshair synchronised across panes.
- Live subscription to `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics: ["delta"]` (plus `["cvd"]`, consumed by S02) over the E23-T02 surface, bootstrapped by `GET /api/v1/market/metrics`; updates **coalesced to 10 Hz** per the SCR-052 performance note.
- **Provisional forming bar** (US-CVD-001 scenario 2): the forming bar's delta updates in real time and is styled as provisional, driven by the `confirm=false` flag from T02 â€” never by a client-side guess about bar boundaries.
- **Gapped bars** (US-CVD-001 scenario 3): bars flagged `gapped` render hatched and are excluded from derived metrics; the exclusion is stated in the legend.
- States from the handoff pack: loading, streaming, stale (shading after 2 s without an update), empty (no recorded tape), error (subscription rejected), and the **partial-history banner naming the first available timestamp** (roadmap R2 exit criterion 5).
- CMP-197 ChartTooltip content on crosshair: time, bar delta, CVD value, and the gapped/provisional flags.
- The **accessible table alternative** entry point in the panel header rendering time / delta / CVD per bar as a real `table` (see Accessibility notes).
- Storybook story **Histogram** for CMP-185, plus states stories (Provisional, Gapped, PartialHistory, Stale).
- Analytics event `cvd.interval_changed`.

## Out of scope
Reset anchors (S02), line/candlestick modes and smoothing (S03), divergence detection and markers (S04/S05), composite multi-symbol CVD (S06, R5), the backend engine and API (T01/T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Histogram renders with a zero line and sign labels
  Given a loaded range of 500 bars for BTCUSDT 1m
  Then each bar's delta renders as a signed histogram bar
  And a zero line is drawn, and the sign is legible as text as well as by bar direction

Scenario: The forming bar is live and marked provisional
  Given the current 1m bar is still forming
  When new prints arrive
  Then the forming bar's delta updates at no more than 10 Hz
  And it is styled as provisional and identified as provisional in the tooltip

Scenario: Gapped bars are hatched and excluded
  Given an ingestion gap covers bars 40 to 44
  Then those bars render hatched
  And they are excluded from derived metrics, and the legend states the exclusion

Scenario: Partial history is named, not implied
  Given the recorder's first available print for the symbol is at 09:12
  And the user requests a range starting at 08:00
  Then a persistent banner names 09:12 as the first available timestamp
  And the series is truncated at 09:12 rather than drawn from zero at 08:00

Scenario: Stale data is shaded
  Given no metrics frame has arrived for 2 seconds
  Then the pane applies the stale shading defined in the handoff pack
  And the shading clears on the next frame

Scenario: A rejected subscription is reported
  Given the server refuses the metrics subscription
  Then the pane renders the error state with the server's reason
  And retry is available without reloading the workspace

Scenario: The time axis stays aligned with the price chart
  When the user pans or zooms the price chart
  Then the delta pane's bars remain aligned to the same time range within one pixel
```

## Technical notes / design
Coalescing: buffer incoming metric points and flush at most once per 100 ms inside the host chart's `requestAnimationFrame` loop â€” do not schedule an independent RAF loop per pane, which is how three open panes would triple the frame cost. The pane reads its geometry from the host chart's time scale; it never computes its own time mapping.

Rendering: the histogram is an instanced quad draw in the engine's existing series pipeline (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`), one instance per bar, with the hatched treatment as a fragment-shader pattern rather than per-bar geometry, so gapped ranges cost nothing extra.

Do not compute delta client-side from a trade stream under any circumstance: US-CVD-001's NFR mandates the shared server-side computation, and a client-side duplicate would drift from footprint and Deep-Stats. The pane renders what `metrics.{symbol}` sends.

## Test plan
- **Unit (frontend):** coalescing buffer flushes at most once per 100 ms and never drops the newest value; state machine loading -> streaming -> stale -> streaming; partial-history banner computation; tooltip content assembly; gapped and provisional flag propagation.
- **Component/Storybook:** Histogram, Provisional, Gapped, PartialHistory, Stale, Error â€” with visual-regression baselines in light, dark, high-contrast and CVD-safe themes.
- **Contract:** mock `metrics.{symbol}` frames validated against the `MetricsUpdate` schema before use, so a server-side schema change breaks the frontend tests loudly.
- **Integration:** REST bootstrap followed by a WS attach renders a continuous series with no duplicated or missing bar at the seam.
- **E2E:** covered by E23-Q02.
- **Coverage:** >=80% frontend lines on the pane package.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.
Specific to this story: the table alternative is the *only* way a screen-reader user reads per-bar delta, so it ships in this story rather than being deferred â€” it must include the gapped and provisional flags as text, and its column headers must be programmatically associated.

## Performance notes
SCR-052 budget (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 Â§Performance): the CVD series updates at a **capped 10 Hz** â€” updates coalesced from the `metrics.{symbol}` stream into one render per 100 ms frame regardless of trade rate; panel budget **<=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU per frame**; **>=58 fps with 3 CVD panels open during a 5,000 trades/min burst**; divergence detection runs incrementally on bar close, never over the whole series. Global budgets (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2): #1 frame time <=16.6 ms p95, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate), #7 frontend memory <=1.5 GB per workspace.
Specific to this story: the histogram draw plus the coalescing buffer must fit inside <=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU with 500 visible bars; measured under E23-Q03.

## Observability
Frontend analytics `cvd.interval_changed`. Client-side performance marks around the pane's draw so the E23-Q03 harness can attribute frame cost to this pane specifically. Log subscription rejections to the client error channel with the server reason code.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via a PR <=400 LOC diff with 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner

- [ ] QA verified against the acceptance criteria; no open P0/P1
- [ ] Storybook stories published and visual-regression baselines approved
- [ ] axe-core clean in CI; manual keyboard pass recorded
- [ ] Design sign-off from the SCR-052 designer (design QA ticket E23-D06)

## Dependencies
`E23-T02` â€” the `metrics.{symbol}` delta/cvd surface and the partial-history and provisional flags; `E23-D05` â€” the signed-off design pack (design-ahead rule: this story cannot start before it is Done); `E11` â€” the pane/axis/crosshair host surface.

title: Cumulative delta with session, UTC-day, never and manual reset anchors
body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-002 â€” Cumulative delta with reset anchors (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want CVD with session, manual or never reset, so that cumulative aggression is meaningful." The roadmap phrases the same requirement as "explicit session/rolling/anchored reset semantics".

The word that carries the weight is *explicit*: a cumulative series whose anchor is ambiguous is worse than no series, because two traders reading the same chart disagree about what they are seeing. Every anchor must therefore be **visible on the chart**, not merely selected in a menu.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** The anchor/reset semantics are computed server-side by `CvdEngine` (E23-T01) and delivered over the existing metrics frames; this story is the anchor selector UI, the anchor marker and the re-request/refresh wiring on top of the pane already shipped in E23-S01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The CVD series itself drawn above the delta histogram in the shared pane, from the `cvd` metric on `metrics.{symbol}`.
- Reset-anchor control in the panel header: `session` / `UTC day` / `never` / `manual`, defaulting to the value the E23-D01 research recommended and the D05 pack recorded.
- **Reset markers** (US-CVD-002 scenario 1): a vertical rule plus a label at each reset, distinct per anchor kind, rendered from the `CvdResetMarker` events emitted by the engine â€” never inferred client-side from a value returning to zero.
- **Manual anchoring** (scenario 2): a bar context action "anchor CVD here" on the price pane and on the CVD pane, plus a keyboard-reachable equivalent from the D01 findings; setting it re-requests the series with `params.cvd.manual_anchor_ts` and the series recomputes from that bar forward.
- **Never-reset start labelling** (scenario 3): the series accumulates across the entire loaded range and the start point is labelled with its timestamp, taken from the server's reported series start (which is the first *available* print, not the first loaded bar).
- The `repairing` state: when the backend is recomputing after a gap (E23-T03), the pane shows the repairing treatment from the handoff pack and does not render a stale cumulative value as if it were current.
- Anchor persistence per pane in the workspace layout (`layout_panes.pane_kind = 'cvd'`, `chart_indicators.indicator_code = 'cvd'` â€” `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`), so a reopened workspace shows the same anchor.
- Analytics events `cvd.mode_changed` and `cvd.anchor_set`.
- Storybook stories: SessionAnchor, NeverAnchorWithStartLabel, ManualAnchor, Repairing.

## Out of scope
Display modes and smoothing (S03), divergence (S04/S05), the backend anchor implementation (T01) and repair (T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Session reset is drawn where it happens
  Given the session anchor at UTC 00:00
  Then CVD resets to zero at that boundary
  And a reset marker with a label is drawn at exactly that timestamp

Scenario: Manual anchor recomputes forward
  Given the user clicks a bar and chooses "anchor CVD here"
  Then CVD recomputes from that bar forward
  And the marker for the manual anchor is drawn at that bar
  And the anchor survives a workspace reload

Scenario: Never-reset labels its start point
  Given the anchor is never
  Then CVD accumulates across the entire loaded range
  And the start point is labelled with the timestamp of the first available print, not the first loaded bar

Scenario: The anchor is always visible
  Given any anchor setting
  Then the active anchor kind and its timestamp appear in the legend
  And they remain visible when the reset marker is scrolled out of view

Scenario: Repair is admitted, not hidden
  Given the backend is recomputing CVD after a WS gap
  Then the pane shows the repairing state

body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-003 â€” CVD display modes (Must)**: "As a trader, I want CVD as a line, histogram or candles, so that I can compare its structure with price." CMP-185's catalogued prop is exactly `displayMode: "candlestick"|"histogram"|"line"`.

Two constraints in the story are unusually specific and must be honoured literally. First, "switching modes is **instant from cached values**" â€” a mode switch is a re-render of data already held, never a refetch. Second, "intrabar CVD OHLC **requires tick data**; without it the mode is **disabled with an explanation**" â€” the mode is not silently missing, and it does not render approximate candles.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** Mode switching is a re-render of values already cached client-side (no refetch, no new engine call); the intrabar-candles mode is a disabled state with an explanation, not a second data path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `line` mode: the CVD series as a polyline in the pane.
- `histogram` mode: CVD drawn as a signed histogram (distinct from the per-bar delta histogram, which remains its own series).
- `candlestick` mode (US-CVD-003 scenario 1): open/high/low/close of CVD within each bar rendered as candles from the intrabar cumulative delta, using the server-computed `cvd_open/high/low/close` from the `min_max_delta` metric â€” the client never derives them.
- **Candles disabled state**: when the server reports `CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE`, the mode option is disabled with a visible explanation naming the reason (no tick data recorded for the requested range) and pointing at the recorder, per the D02/D03 state design.
- **EMA smoothing** (scenario 3): a configurable EMA overlay (default period 9) drawn **on top of** the raw series, which remains visible; the legend states the smoothing parameters.
- Mode and smoothing persisted per pane in the workspace layout alongside the anchor from S02.
- Instant switching: all three representations are derived from one cached series in memory; a mode change issues no network request.
- Storybook stories completing CMP-185's catalogued set: **Line**, **Candlestick** (Histogram shipped in S01), plus SmoothedOverlay and CandlesDisabled.
- Analytics `cvd.mode_changed`.

## Out of scope
Divergence (S04/S05), composite CVD (S06), the backend intrabar computation (T01) and its availability determination (K01/T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: CVD candles are built from the intrabar path
  Given a bar with cvd_open 100, min_delta -3, max_delta 20 and delta 12
  Then the CVD candle renders with open 100, low 97, high 120 and close 112
  And those values come from the server, not from a client-side derivation

Scenario: Switching modes is instant and offline
  Given a loaded CVD series
  When the user switches between line, histogram and candlestick
  Then the new representation renders from cached values within one frame
  And no network request is issued

Scenario: Candles are disabled with a reason, never approximated
  Given the server reports CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE for the requested range
  Then the candlestick option is disabled
  And an explanation names the reason and is reachable by keyboard
  And no approximate candle is drawn

Scenario: Smoothing supplements rather than replaces
  Given EMA smoothing of 9 is enabled
  Then a smoothed overlay renders and the raw series remains visible
  And the legend states the smoothing kind and period

Scenario: Mode persists across reload
  Given candlestick mode and EMA 9 are selected
  When the workspace is closed and reopened
  Then the pane restores both settings
```

## Technical notes / design
Keep one in-memory series of `CvdPoint` carrying `{t, cvd, cvd_open, cvd_high, cvd_low, delta, confirm, gapped}`; the three display modes are three draw paths over that one buffer. This is what makes switching free and is the reason the mode must not be a subscription parameter.

Candle rendering reuses the engine's existing candle series pipeline from E12 rather than a bespoke path â€” CVD candles are geometrically identical to price candles with a different value axis.

The EMA is computed client-side over the cached confirmed bars **or** consumed from the server's smoothed series, whichever the T01 implementation exposes; whichever is chosen, gapped bars are excluded from the EMA input (they are excluded from derived metrics by US-CVD-001) and the discontinuity is drawn as a break, not bridged.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** candle geometry from (cvd_open, min_delta, max_delta, delta) including `min == max == 0`; EMA warm-up and gapped-bar exclusion; mode switch issues zero network calls (asserted with a mocked transport); persistence round-trip.
- **Component/Storybook:** Line, Candlestick, SmoothedOverlay, CandlesDisabled with visual-regression baselines across four themes.
- **Integration:** a range with no recorded tick data yields the disabled state end to end from the server's reason code.
- **Perf:** mode switch measured to complete within one frame at 500 visible bars (E23-Q03 harness).
- **Coverage:** >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

The smoothing period input is a labelled numeric field with a stated range.

title: Single-bar delta divergence flags with threshold control and (estimated) chip
body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-004 â€” Single-bar divergence detection (Should)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want bars where price and delta disagree flagged, so that I spot absorption." A bar that closes up on strongly negative delta is the classic absorption signature â€” buyers lifted the offer and price still could not hold, or sellers absorbed the buying.

This is the first `(estimated)` surface in the epic. CVD itself is exact (Bybit publishes the aggressor side), but "price and delta disagree **beyond a threshold**" is a heuristic with a tunable parameter, and R2 exit criterion 4 is unambiguous: "Every estimated view carries the (estimated) badge and a popover explaining the heuristic and its failure modes. A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic."

The NFR also makes this story a producer for other epics: "flags emitted as **events for alerts and rules**" â€” E40 Alerts and E35's `cvd_divergence` metric consume them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Single-bar divergence evaluation on **bar close only** (never on the forming bar, US-CVD-004 scenario 3), flagging bars where the close direction and the sign of delta disagree and `abs(delta)` exceeds the configured threshold.
- Flag rendering: a glyph **and a text label** (scenario 1) on the affected bar, in both the delta histogram and the CVD series.
- **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** on the divergence feature, with a popover stating the heuristic, the active threshold, and the known failure modes (thin books, single large prints, bars straddling a session boundary) â€” copy taken from the E23-D05 pack, not invented at build time.
- Threshold control (scenario 2): changing the delta-magnitude threshold recomputes flags over the loaded range, incrementally where possible and never blocking the frame loop.
- Flags emitted as **events** on the client event bus in the shape E40/E35 consume, and listed as text in the accessible table alternative and in the SCR-052 divergence text line.
- Persistence of the threshold and the on/off state per pane in the workspace layout.
- Storybook stories: SingleBarDivergence, DivergenceEstimatedPopover, ThresholdChanged.
- Analytics `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked`.

## Out of scope
Multi-bar swing divergence (S05 â€” a different detector with a different confirmation rule), alert delivery (E40), rule evaluation (E35), backend persistence of divergence events.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An absorption bar is flagged
  Given a bar closes up while its delta is strongly negative beyond the threshold
  Then the bar is flagged with a glyph and a text label
  And the flag appears in the accessible table alternative as a text row

Scenario: Threshold changes recompute the loaded range
  Given flags are displayed with a threshold of 50
  When the threshold is changed to 200
  Then flags recompute over the loaded range
  And the active threshold is shown in the legend

Scenario: The forming bar is never flagged
  Given the current bar's delta already exceeds the threshold and disagrees with its direction
  Then it is not flagged while it is forming
  And it is evaluated once, on close

Scenario: The estimated badge and popover are present and accurate
  Then the divergence feature carries the (estimated) chip
  And its popover names the heuristic, the active threshold and at least three failure modes
  And the popover is reachable and dismissible by keyboard

Scenario: Flags are emitted as events
  When a bar is flagged
  Then a divergence event carrying symbol, bar timestamp, delta and threshold is published on the event bus

Scenario: Gapped bars are never flagged

The one exception is a threshold change, which is a bounded re-scan of the loaded range; run it in a chunked task yielding to the frame loop so a slider drag cannot stall rendering, and debounce the control.

Emit-once semantics: keep a set of already-emitted `(symbol, bar_ts)` keys so re-renders, mode switches and anchor changes do not republish events into the alert path. This is the difference between a useful alert and an alert the user mutes.

The detector's inputs and thresholds must be visible in an inspector â€” R2 Â§6.2 requires that "every detector exposes its inputs and thresholds in an inspector so the user can see *why* it fired", and while that sentence is written about E25, the honesty gate in Â§6.4 applies to every estimated view.

title: Multi-bar swing divergence between price and CVD with no repainting
body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-005 â€” Multi-bar swing divergence detection (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want swing-based divergence between price and CVD, so that I see structural disagreement." Price makes a higher high while CVD makes a lower high; the connector between the two swing pairs is the classic bearish divergence.

The NFR is the whole story: "uses the **same confirmed-swing source as US-IND-005**; **no repainting after confirmation**." US-IND-005 (Zig Zag, E13) already exposes confirmed swing highs and lows as named metrics, and its own NFR states "no rule may act on a provisional swing â€” enforced in the rule engine, covered by tests". E23 must consume that source. Building a second swing detector here would produce two definitions of a swing in one product, which is how a chart and an alert come to disagree in front of a user.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Swing-divergence detection between the price series and the CVD series using the **confirmed-swing source from E13 / US-IND-005** â€” consumed, not reimplemented.
- Bearish divergence (scenario 1): price makes a higher swing high while CVD makes a lower swing high -> a connector is drawn between the two swing pairs (one connector on the price pane, one on the CVD pane, visually associated) with a label. Bullish divergence is the mirror case (lower swing low on price, higher swing low on CVD).
- **Confirmation rule** (scenario 2): a divergence is drawn only once **both** swings are confirmed by the swing detector, never on provisional swings â€” and once drawn it never moves or disappears (the no-repaint guarantee).
- **Configurable lookback** (scenario 3): changing the swing lookback recomputes detection, and the **active parameters are shown in the legend**.
- CMP-227 `(estimated)` chip and popover for swing divergence, with its own failure modes (lookback sensitivity, sparse swings in a trending market, divergence that persists for many bars).
- Divergence text events in the SCR-052 divergence line and the accessible table alternative, in the same event shape as S04 so alerts and rules consume one stream.
- Persistence of the lookback and the on/off state per pane.
- Storybook stories: BearishSwingDivergence, BullishSwingDivergence, ProvisionalSwingNotDrawn, LookbackChanged. (Together with S04 these complete CMP-185's catalogued **WithDivergenceMarkers** story.)

## Out of scope
Implementing swing detection (E13 owns it â€” a PR adding a swing algorithm here is rejected on sight), alert delivery (E40), rule evaluation (E35), single-bar divergence (S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bearish divergence is drawn between confirmed swing pairs
  Given price makes a higher swing high while CVD makes a lower swing high
  And both swings are confirmed by the swing detector
  Then a connector is drawn between the two swing pairs with a label

Scenario: Bullish divergence is the mirror case
  Given price makes a lower swing low while CVD makes a higher swing low
  And both swings are confirmed
  Then a connector is drawn with a label identifying it as bullish

Scenario: Provisional swings are never drawn
  Given the most recent price swing is still provisional
  Then no divergence involving it is drawn
  And it appears once, when the swing is confirmed

Scenario: Nothing repaints after confirmation
  Given a divergence has been drawn
  When further bars arrive and the market extends the move
  Then the existing connector does not move, change endpoints or disappear

Scenario: Lookback change recomputes and is disclosed
  When the swing lookback is changed
  Then detection recomputes over the loaded range
  And the active parameters are shown in the legend

Scenario: The swing source is shared
  When the implementation is reviewed
  Then it consumes the confirmed-swing metrics from the indicators framework
  And contains no independent swing-detection algorithm
```

## Technical notes / design
Subscribe to the confirmed swing metrics exposed by E13's Zig Zag (US-IND-005 scenario 2: "confirmed swing highs and lows are exposed as named metrics"). Detection then reduces to pairing the last two confirmed swing highs (or lows) on each series and comparing directions â€” a small, testable pure function over two swing lists.

No-repaint is an architectural property, not a coding-style preference: once a divergence is emitted it is appended to an immutable list keyed by `(price_swing_ts, cvd_swing_ts)`. Recomputation on a lookback change clears and rebuilds the list wholesale (the user asked for different parameters, so a change is expected and disclosed); nothing else may mutate it.

Association across panes: the price-pane connector and the CVD-pane connector share an id so hovering or focusing one highlights the other â€” SCR-052's job is to make the *disagreement* visible, which requires both halves to be legible as one object.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** the divergence predicate over a table of swing-pair fixtures (higher-high/lower-high, lower-low/higher-low, equal highs, single swing available, no swings); provisional-swing exclusion; the no-repaint invariant asserted by feeding a bar stream forward and asserting the emitted list is append-only; lookback recompute clears and rebuilds deterministically.
- **Property:** for any bar stream, replaying it in full and feeding it incrementally produce the same divergence list (this is the client-side analogue of the determinism gate).
- **Component/Storybook:** four stories with visual-regression baselines; cross-pane association asserted.
- **Integration:** with E13's swing metrics from a recorded fixture containing at least two confirmed divergences.
- **E2E:** covered by E23-Q02.
- **Coverage:** >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes

The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

The `(estimated)` chip follows the S04 popover pattern.

SCR-052 budget (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 Â§Performance): the CVD series updates at a **capped 10 Hz** â€” updates coalesced from the `metrics.{symbol}` stream into one render per 100 ms frame regardless of trade rate; panel budget **<=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU per frame**; **>=58 fps with 3 CVD panels open during a 5,000 trades/min burst**; divergence detection runs incrementally on bar close, never over the whole series. Global budgets (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2): #1 frame time <=16.6 ms p95, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate), #7 frontend memory <=1.5 GB per workspace.
Specific to this story: detection runs on swing confirmation only â€” at most a handful of evaluations per minute â€” so its steady-state cost must be effectively zero; only the lookback-change rebuild is bounded work and it must be chunked like S04's threshold re-scan.

## Observability
Analytics `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked` (shared with S04, distinguished by a `kind` property). Counter of swing divergences emitted per session per kind, feeding the same flood detection as S04.

title: Composite normalised CVD across up to five symbols
body:
## Context
Implements **US-CVD-006 â€” Composite / normalised CVD (Could)**: "As a trader, I want normalised CVD across several symbols, so that I can see market-wide aggression."

This story is **deliberately deferred to R5**. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§12 (descoping ladder) lists it as descope candidate 4: "Multi-symbol CVD comparison â€” **E23 CVD & delta panes**". It is a *Could* in the story catalogue, it is the only part of the epic not needed for the R2 exit criteria, and its backend cost (a cross-symbol streaming series) is disproportionate to its value at beta. It is therefore planned at sprint `Backlog` and scheduled into R5 only if the train has room. It is written in full here so that, if it is pulled in, it is ready â€” not so that it is quietly built in Sprint 12.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** Composite CVD reuses the S03 rendering path and the S01 pane wholesale; the net-new work is the symbol picker, the normalisation transform and the multi-series legend. It remains R5-deferred (sprint `Backlog`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Symbol selection for the composite (up to **5** symbols, US-CVD-006 scenario 3) from the recorded-symbol set.
- Per-symbol CVD **normalisation** by z-score over a configurable lookback, and a composite series plotted from the normalised components, with each component individually toggleable (scenario 1).
- **Backend-side computation** (NFR: "composite computed backend-side and streamed as one series") â€” a composite metric served over the existing `metrics.{symbol}` family surface, not N client subscriptions summed in the browser.
- **Missing-data handling** (scenario 2): a symbol lacking recorded prints for part of the range is excluded for that portion, and the exclusion is shown in the legend with the affected interval â€” consistent with the epic-wide rule that gaps are admitted, never smoothed.
- **Limit enforcement** (scenario 3): selecting more than 5 symbols is refused with an explanation of the performance limit, both client-side for usability and server-side as the authoritative control.
- Legend showing the components, their weights (equal by default), the lookback and the excluded intervals.
- Storybook stories: Composite2Symbols, ComponentToggled, PartialExclusion, LimitRefused.

## Out of scope
Everything in R2: this story must not be started before the R2 train has closed and the R5 capacity decision has been made. Cross-venue composites (single exchange only). Any weighting scheme beyond equal weights.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Composite of two symbols
  Given BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT are selected
  Then each CVD is normalised as a z-score over the configured lookback
  And the composite is plotted with its components individually toggleable

Scenario: Missing data excludes rather than distorts
  Given ETHUSDT lacks recorded prints between 10:00 and 10:20
  Then ETHUSDT is excluded from the composite for that interval
  And the legend shows the exclusion and names the interval

Scenario: The symbol limit is enforced on both sides
  Given five symbols are already selected
  When a sixth is chosen
  Then the selection is refused with an explanation of the performance limit
  And a request that bypasses the client is refused by the server as well

Scenario: One series on the wire
  When the composite is streamed
  Then it arrives as a single computed series
  And the client issues no per-symbol CVD subscription for the purpose of building it
```

## Technical notes / design
Z-score normalisation over a lookback window `n`: `z_i = (cvd_i - mean(cvd[i-n..i])) / stddev(cvd[i-n..i])`, with the degenerate zero-variance window emitting zero rather than an infinity or a NaN â€” that case is common in a thin overnight session and is exactly where a naive implementation renders a spike that a trader would read as signal.

The composite is `mean(z_i)` over the currently enabled components at each timestamp, computed over the intersection of available timestamps, with excluded intervals carried as explicit exclusion ranges rather than as nulls in the value series.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** z-score including the zero-variance window; composite over partially-overlapping timestamp sets; exclusion-range computation; the 5-symbol limit.
- **Integration:** backend composite equals an offline recomputation over the same recorded symbols (the parity discipline of E23-T04 extends to this series).
- **Component/Storybook:** four stories.
- **Coverage:** >=80% frontend, >=85% on the backend composite module.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.
The composite multiplies the per-request cost by the symbol count, which makes the 5-symbol cap a **denial-of-service control**, not only a performance limit â€” hence the requirement that it be enforced server-side and covered by an abuse case in E23-X02 if this story is pulled in.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.
Specific to this story: component toggles are labelled checkboxes; excluded intervals are listed as text in the legend and in the table alternative; the composite series is distinguishable from its components by line style as well as colour.

## Performance notes
SCR-052 budget (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 Â§Performance): the CVD series updates at a **capped 10 Hz** â€” updates coalesced from the `metrics.{symbol}` stream into one render per 100 ms frame regardless of trade rate; panel budget **<=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU per frame**; **>=58 fps with 3 CVD panels open during a 5,000 trades/min burst**; divergence detection runs incrementally on bar close, never over the whole series. Global budgets (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2): #1 frame time <=16.6 ms p95, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate), #7 frontend memory <=1.5 GB per workspace.
Specific to this story: the composite must not increase the pane's per-frame cost beyond the single-symbol budget â€” it is one series on the wire regardless of component count.

## Observability
`cv_cvd_composite_requests_total{symbols}`, `cv_cvd_composite_refused_total{reason="symbol_limit"}`. Analytics event on component toggle.

- [ ] Scheduled into an R5 sprint by explicit decision before work starts; not started during R2

- The **honesty checklist** for this epic, per the roadmap Â§6.4 Honesty gate: for each estimated view (single-bar divergence, swing divergence) â€” badge present, popover accurate, thresholds/parameters visible.
- The **regression pack** definition: which cases run every sprint thereafter.

```

## Technical notes / design
Test-case design should lean on **oracles**, not eyeballs: the strongest oracle in this epic is the offline DuckDB recomputation (E23-T04), so black-box cases that assert a displayed value should assert it against that oracle rather than against a tester's judgement. The second oracle is the uninterrupted-run comparison for reconnect cases.

title: Playwright E2E suite for the CVD pane: anchors, modes and divergence
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E at the top of the pyramid: few, high-value, user-visible journeys. For E23 the journeys worth automating are the ones where a silent wrong value is possible â€” anchors, reconnect and divergence â€” plus the honesty checks the roadmap makes release-blocking.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright (web + Electron) specs added to the existing E2E suite:
  1. **Open the CVD pane and read a value**: add SCR-052 to a workspace, load a recorded range, assert the displayed CVD at a known bar equals the golden value from the E23-T04 fixture.
  2. **Anchor journeys**: switch session -> UTC day -> never, asserting the reset markers, the never-anchor start label, and the legend disclosure; set a manual anchor by clicking a bar; reload the workspace and assert it persists.
  3. **Display modes**: switch line -> histogram -> candlestick asserting no network request is issued (route interception) and the rendered mode changes; enable EMA 9 and assert the raw series remains present; load a range without tick data and assert the candlestick option is disabled with an explanation.
  4. **Divergence**: drive a fixture containing a known single-bar divergence and a known swing divergence; assert the glyph, the label, the `(estimated)` chip, the popover content, and the entries in the divergence list; advance the stream and assert the swing connector **does not move** (no-repaint).
  5. **Gapped and partial history**: assert hatching on gapped bars and the partial-history banner naming the first available timestamp.
  6. **Reconnect**: sever the WS at the proxy, reconnect, and assert the post-repair displayed CVD equals the uninterrupted golden value (the UI half of E23-T03's guarantee).
  7. **Table alternative**: open it from the panel header by keyboard and assert it contains the per-bar delta, CVD and divergence rows.
- Deterministic fixture driving: all specs run against a replayed recorded window, never a live market.
- CI wiring into the existing E2E job with the epic's specs tagged so they can be run alone.

## Out of scope
Unit and component tests (owned by the stories), performance (Q03), a11y audit depth (Q04), chaos scenarios (Q06) â€” though spec 6 overlaps deliberately, because the user-visible half of reconnect correctness belongs in E2E.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  When the suite runs ten times against the same fixture
  Then it passes ten times with no flakes
  And no spec depends on a wall-clock sleep in place of a state assertion

Scenario: Displayed values are asserted against the oracle
  Then every value assertion compares against the golden fixture from the parity harness
  And no assertion encodes a hand-typed expected number without a fixture reference

Scenario: The no-repaint guarantee is automated
  Given a drawn swing divergence
  When 50 further bars are replayed
  Then the connector endpoints are unchanged

Scenario: The honesty checks are automated
  Then the suite asserts the presence of the (estimated) chip and the popover text for both divergence kinds
  And a missing badge fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive the WS from a controllable replay endpoint rather than mocking in the browser, so the specs exercise the real decode path (MessagePack envelope, `MetricsUpdate` frames) â€” a browser-level mock would pass while a protocol change broke production.

Use the engine's exposed test hooks for canvas assertions rather than pixel comparison where possible: the CVD pane is WebGL, so assert against the DOM mirror and the table alternative for content, and reserve visual snapshots for the Storybook layer where they are stable.

## Test plan
Meta: the suite's own reliability is the deliverable. Each spec must fail when the corresponding behaviour is deliberately broken â€” verified once, at review, by mutation (e.g. disable the no-repaint invariant and confirm spec 4 fails).

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes

SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. - **Worst-case scene check**: the full R2 order-flow scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + **CVD pane**, roadmap exit criterion 2) with the CVD pane's marginal contribution isolated, asserting p95 <=16.6 ms and no frame below the 30 fps floor.
- **WS tick -> screen latency** measurement for the `metrics.{symbol}` path specifically, per the Â§5.1 methodology (backend receipt timestamp vs the frontend `requestAnimationFrame` paint), asserting p95 <100 ms and p99 <250 ms.

Fixing regressions (separate tickets), functional E2E (Q02), chaos (Q06), the footprint/heatmap benchmarks owned by E18/E21.

Each benchmark runs 5 times; the committed baseline is the median p95. The harness is self-testing: a deliberately inserted 3 ms delay in the pane draw must fail the gate, verified at review.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-052 including the table alternative
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` mandates WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and **manual screen-reader passes**, and the R2 quality gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4) requires an a11y pass on every new view. SCR-052 is a WebGL surface, so it depends entirely on the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) â€” the table alternative is not a courtesy, it is the only channel through which a screen-reader user receives per-bar delta and CVD.

The audit basis is the checklist produced by E23-D04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Automated axe-core pass over SCR-052 in all states (loading, streaming, stale, empty, error, partial history, repairing, candles-disabled, divergence popover open) with zero violations.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA + Firefox and VoiceOver + Safari covering: reaching the pane, reaching the table alternative from the panel header, reading per-bar delta/CVD/divergence rows, operating the anchor / mode / smoothing / divergence controls, opening and dismissing the `(estimated)` popover with focus returning correctly, and hearing each divergence as a discrete text event.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: full operation of every control and both divergence inspections without a mouse, including setting a manual anchor from the table alternative (E23-S02's keyboard requirement).
- **Contrast and non-colour encoding verification** in light, dark, high-contrast and the CVD-safe themes at 100% and 150% font scales: text >=4.5:1, series strokes and focus indicators >=3:1, and confirmation that the sign of delta is readable without hue.
- **Reduced-motion verification** against the E23-D04 motion spec.
- Findings report with severity, each mapped to a WCAG success criterion, and defect tickets filed.
- Sign-off (or refusal with the blocking list) from the accessibility specialist.

## Out of scope
Fixing the findings (separate `fix/` tickets), visual design QA (E23-D06), functional E2E (Q02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated checks are clean in every state
  When axe-core runs against SCR-052 in each of its states
  Then zero violations are reported
  And the state list matches the states enumerated in the design pack

Scenario: A screen-reader user can read the data
  Given NVDA with Firefox
  When the user opens the table alternative from the panel header
  Then per-bar time, delta, CVD and divergence flags are announced with their column headers
  And gapped and provisional bars are identified as such in text

Scenario: A keyboard user can set a manual anchor
  Given focus is in the table alternative on a bar row
  When the anchor action is invoked
  Then the CVD anchor is set at that bar and the change is announced once

Scenario: The estimated popover is operable
  When the (estimated) chip is activated from the keyboard
  Then focus moves into the popover, Escape dismisses it, and focus returns to the chip

Scenario: Colour is never the only carrier
  Given the CVD-safe themes under deuteranopia simulation

Scenario: Streaming does not flood assistive technology
  Given the series is updating at 10 Hz
  Then no live region announces the streaming values
```

## Technical notes / design
Audit against a replayed fixture so every state is reproducible; auditing a live feed means the gapped and partial-history states may never appear during the session. Record the sessions so findings can be reviewed without re-running them.

## Test plan
The axe-core state sweep is automated and added to CI (it becomes a permanent guard, not a one-time audit). The manual passes are scripted so they are repeatable at R5 for the regression audit.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

## Performance notes
Verify the table alternative does not itself become a performance problem: it must render the visible range, virtualised, not the whole loaded series, and must not update at stream rate.

## Observability
Findings are recorded in the accessibility defect register with WCAG criterion tags so the R5 a11y epic (E46-adjacent hardening) can see the trend.

- [ ] axe-core state sweep added to CI and green
- [ ] Both manual screen-reader passes completed and recorded

- [ ] Defects filed; accessibility specialist sign-off recorded

`E23-S04` and `E23-S05` â€” the divergence popovers and events are a large part of the audit surface; `E23-D04` â€” the checklist that defines pass and fail.

title: Chaos scenarios: WS gaps, recorder holes and repair storms on the CVD path
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) and the R2 integration gate names the fixtures: "normal session, high-volatility burst, **WS disconnect + resync**, **sequence gap**, thin-book symbol". For CVD these are not generic resilience tests â€” they are correctness tests, because the failure mode of this epic is a value that is wrong forever and looks fine.

## Scope / Deliverables
Automated chaos scenarios against the CVD path, each asserting the post-event series equals the uninterrupted golden series from E23-T04:
1. **Clean disconnect + reconnect** of the upstream trade stream for 45 s during active trading.
2. **Sequence gap without a disconnect** (frames dropped in transit) detected by the Â§7 sequence numbers.
3. **Disconnect straddling a session anchor**, so the repair window contains a reset â€” the case where a naive repair re-bases the series.
4. **Disconnect while the recorder is also down**, producing a genuine hole: assert the bars are flagged `gapped`, excluded from derived metrics, surfaced to the UI, and **not interpolated**.
5. **Repair storm**: five disconnect/reconnect cycles within one minute, asserting repairs coalesce, the queue depth stays bounded, and the final value is still exact.
6. **Disconnect during an in-flight repair**, asserting the repair window extends rather than a second repair starting.
7. **Oversize gap** exceeding `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints`, asserting a bounded refusal, the `gapped` flag, the counter increment and the alert â€” not an unbounded scan.
8. **Exchange 5xx and rate-limit 10018** during the repair's historical fetch, asserting backoff and eventual correctness.
9. **Client-side reconnect** (browser loses the WS but the backend is healthy), asserting the client re-snapshots rather than resuming a delta stream onto stale state.
- Each scenario runs in CI against a replayed fixture; scenarios 1-4 also run in the pre-release soak.
- A written resilience report for the R2 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
Book resync chaos (E21/E08), replay-engine chaos (E26), the repair implementation itself (E23-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every fault produces the exact value
  Given any of scenarios 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 or 9
  Then the post-event CVD series equals the uninterrupted golden series bar for bar, to the last decimal

Scenario: A real hole is admitted
  Given the recorder was down during the gap
  Then the affected bars are flagged gapped and excluded from derived metrics
  And no interpolated value is emitted or displayed

Scenario: Repairs coalesce under a storm
  Given five disconnect cycles within one minute
  Then the repair count is lower than the disconnect count
  And the repair queue depth never exceeds its configured bound
  And the final value is exact

Scenario: An oversize repair is refused loudly
  Given a gap window exceeding the configured print clamp
  Then the repair is refused, the range is flagged gapped, the refusal counter increments and an alert fires
  And no unbounded query is issued

Scenario: Upstream errors do not corrupt state
  Given the historical fetch returns 5xx and then rate-limit 10018
  Then the repair backs off and retries
  And on eventual success the series is exact
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection at the proxy layer (sever, delay, drop selected frames) rather than inside the application, so the test exercises the real detection path. The golden comparison is the same oracle E23-T04 built â€” chaos tests assert correctness, not merely absence of crash, and that is the entire point of this ticket.

Scenario 4 requires the ability to stop the recorder mid-fixture; coordinate with E16's test hooks rather than deleting data files underneath a running system.

## Test plan
Each scenario is a test case with a deterministic seed; the suite runs nightly and before each release cut. Flakiness is treated as a product defect until proven otherwise â€” a non-deterministic repair is exactly the bug this epic most fears.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.
Scenarios 5 and 7 are simultaneously **resilience and security** tests: they are the DoS abuse cases from E23-X01 executed as chaos. Results are shared with E23-X02 rather than duplicated.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.
Scenario 4's UI half (the gapped and repairing states being perceivable) is covered by E23-Q02 and E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Assert that live accumulation for *other* symbols is unaffected during a repair (no head-of-line blocking) and that per-symbol CPU returns to budget #11 after the repair completes.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected metric movement: `cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total`, `cv_cvd_repair_queue_depth`, `cv_cvd_gapped_bars_total`. A scenario that passes without moving its metric is treated as not having exercised the path.

Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:

title: STRIDE threat model for the CVD & delta panes epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a **STRIDE threat model per epic**, produced before implementation so its controls are requirements rather than retrofits. E23 handles no credentials and no order entry, so its risk profile is narrow but not empty: it introduces a **server-side recomputation triggered by client-controlled parameters** and a **fan-out subscription whose cost scales with the client's option choices**. Both are resource-amplification surfaces, and the R2 security gate already flags "unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector" for E21 â€” the same class of issue appears here in a different shape.

The model must be written before E23-T01 and E23-T02, which is why it is scheduled in Sprint 10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model over the epic's data flows: Bybit `publicTrade` -> ingestion -> M9 aggregation -> `CvdEngine` -> `orderflow_metrics` (QuestDB) / Parquet -> `metrics.{symbol}` fan-out and `GET /market/metrics` -> the SCR-052 pane.
- Per-element analysis with, at minimum, these threats enumerated and rated:
  - **(D)** Subscription amplification: `metrics.{symbol}` with 12 metrics x many symbols x minimum `throttle_ms` multiplying backend CPU and egress.
  - **(D)** Recompute amplification: a client repeatedly changing the anchor (or setting distant manual anchors) forcing large historical scans over QuestDB and Parquet.
  - **(D)** Repair storm amplification: an upstream that flaps driving unbounded repair work.
  - **(D)** Unbounded range: `from`/`to` on `/market/metrics` spanning the entire retention window.
  - **(T)** Parameter tampering: `manual_anchor_ts`, smoothing period, swing lookback and the `params` JSON (max 2048 chars) used unvalidated in query construction or as allocation sizes.
  - **(T)** Malformed `params` JSON as a parser-level attack surface.
  - **(I)** RBAC: confirm `marketdata:read` is enforced on every new code path, including the WS subscribe path, and that a Viewer role sees market data but cannot cause a recompute if that is the intended boundary.
  - **(R)** Repudiation: whether anchor changes and recompute triggers need audit entries (market-data reads are not audited in general; a decision is required and recorded).
  - **(S)** Spoofing is out of scope for this epic (no new authentication surface) â€” recorded explicitly as considered and dismissed with a reason.
- Controls mapped to the tickets that must implement them: clamps and caps in E23-T02, the print clamp and coalescing queue in E23-T03, the client-side pre-validation in E23-S02.
- Abuse cases handed to E23-X02 for execution and to E23-Q06 for the chaos overlap.
- Data classification statement: market data, internal, no PII, no secrets â€” and the consequent handling rules for fixtures (E23-T04's golden fixtures must contain no account or key material).

## Out of scope
Implementation of controls (the referenced tickets), penetration testing (R4, E43), the book/DOM subscription model (E21's own model).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The model covers every element of the flow
  When the model is reviewed against the data-flow diagram
  Then every process, data store, data flow and trust boundary has a STRIDE analysis
  And every threat has a rating and either a control or an explicit accepted-risk record

Scenario: Controls become requirements
  Then each control names the ticket that implements it and the acceptance criterion that proves it
  And no control is left assigned to the epic in general

Scenario: Amplification is quantified, not just named
  Given the subscription and recompute amplification threats
  Then the model states the worst-case resource multiplier for each
  And the chosen clamp values are justified against it

Scenario: Dismissals are recorded
  Given a STRIDE category judged not applicable
  Then the model records the category, the judgement and the reason
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the data-flow diagram from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` as the base and annotate the M9 CVD path; do not draw a new architecture. Trust boundaries that matter: browser -> API/WS gateway (untrusted input), application -> QuestDB/Parquet (query construction), ingestion -> application (untrusted upstream â€” Bybit is not an attacker but it is not a guarantee either).

Clamp values should be derived from the measurements in E23-K01 where they exist, so `max_recompute_prints` is a number with a basis rather than a round figure.

## Test plan
The model is reviewed by the security engineer and the architect. Its outputs are testable by construction: each control's acceptance criterion is asserted in the implementing ticket, and the abuse cases are executed in E23-X02 and E23-Q06.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
The clamps this model mandates directly bound the epic's worst-case resource use; they must be set so that legitimate use (a full trading day at 1-minute bars, a manual anchor anywhere in the loaded range) is never refused. A control that blocks normal use will be disabled in production and is therefore not a control.

## Observability
Mandates the rejection and refusal counters (`cv_metrics_subscription_rejected_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total{reason}`) and requires that refusals are logged with enough context to distinguish an attack from a misconfigured client.

title: Security review and abuse-case testing of the CVD metrics surface
body:
## Context
Closes the security loop opened by E23-X01: the controls the threat model required are now implemented in E23-T02 (clamps, caps, validation) and E23-T03 (print clamp, repair coalescing), and this ticket verifies them adversarially rather than by inspection. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a security review per epic before the train's PRR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of the diff across `server/orderflow/cvd/`, the `/market/metrics` handler and the `metrics.{symbol}` subscribe path, against the E23-X01 control list.
- **Abuse-case execution**:
  1. Subscription amplification â€” maximum metrics x maximum symbols x minimum `throttle_ms`; assert clamping or refusal and that the service stays within its resource envelope.
  2. Recompute amplification â€” rapid repeated anchor changes and distant manual anchors; assert debouncing, clamping and bounded query cost.
  3. Unbounded range â€” `from`/`to` spanning the full retention window on `/market/metrics`; assert the range clamp and a clear error.
  4. Parameter tampering â€” `manual_anchor_ts` outside the range, negative and enormous smoothing periods and swing lookbacks, a `params` string at and beyond the 2048-char limit, malformed and deeply-nested JSON, unexpected metric codes; assert 422 with a safe error and no stack trace.
  5. Injection surface â€” any client parameter reaching a QuestDB or DuckDB query must be parameterised; attempt SQL-metacharacter payloads in `symbol`, `param` and the `params` values.
  6. RBAC â€” assert every new path enforces `marketdata:read`, and that an unauthenticated WS subscribe and REST call are both refused.
  7. Repair-storm abuse (shared execution with E23-Q06 scenarios 5 and 7).
- **SAST/DAST rules**: confirm CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit cover the new modules; add a Semgrep rule if the review finds a pattern worth banning repo-wide (e.g. string-interpolated time-series queries). Add the `/market/metrics` endpoint to the OWASP ZAP DAST profile with its parameter set.
- **SCA**: confirm no new dependency was introduced by this epic; if one was, record its licence and vulnerability status.
- Findings report with severities, remediation tickets filed, and a security sign-off (or refusal with the blocking list).

## Out of scope
Penetration testing (R4, E43), the chaos scenarios themselves (E23-Q06 executes them; this ticket consumes the results of 5 and 7), threat modelling (X01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control is verified
  When the review is complete
  Then each control from the E23-X01 model has a verification result of pass or fail
  And every fail has a remediation ticket with an owner and a severity

Scenario: Amplification is bounded in practice
  Given the maximum-amplification subscription and the rapid-anchor-change abuse cases
  Then the service clamps or refuses
  And its CPU and memory stay within the configured envelope throughout

Scenario: Tampered parameters fail safely
  Given out-of-range, oversized, malformed and injection-shaped parameters
  Then every request is rejected with a 422 and a safe message
  And no stack trace, query text or internal path is disclosed

Scenario: Queries are parameterised
  When client-supplied values reaching the time-series queries are reviewed
  Then all are bound parameters
  And SQL-metacharacter payloads produce a validation error, never a query error

Scenario: RBAC is enforced on every new path
  Given an unauthenticated client
  Then both the REST bootstrap and the WS subscribe are refused
  And a client without marketdata:read is refused on both

Scenario: Static and dynamic analysis cover the new code
  Then CodeQL, Semgrep and Bandit report on the new modules with zero unresolved high findings
  And the ZAP profile includes /market/metrics with its parameters
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the abuse cases against staging with resource monitoring attached, so "the clamp worked" is demonstrated by a flat resource graph rather than by an absent error. Reuse the k6 script from E23-Q03 for case 1 rather than writing a second load generator.

Injection testing must target the *time-series* query paths specifically â€” QuestDB and DuckDB are less familiar to most reviewers than Postgres, and a parameterisation gap is likelier there.

## Test plan
Each abuse case is scripted and retained in the security test suite so it runs again at R4's pen-test preparation rather than being a one-off exercise. A case that cannot be scripted is documented as a manual procedure with steps.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.
This ticket additionally verifies: no secret, key or account identifier appears in the epic's logs, metrics labels or golden fixtures; `symbol` labels on Prometheus metrics are bounded by the recorded-symbol set so metric cardinality is not a client-controlled amplification vector in its own right.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Resource envelopes are asserted against the same budgets E23-Q03 measured (#6, #11, #13); an abuse case that stays functional but breaches a budget is a finding, not a pass.

## Observability
Verifies that every refusal path increments its counter and logs with a reason, and that the counters are on a dashboard with an alert â€” an unmonitored control is indistinguishable from no control during an incident.

## Dependencies
`E23-X01` â€” the control list being verified; `E23-T02` and `E23-T03` â€” the implementations under review.

title: Assert CvdEngine/delta aggregation exclusion from the statechart catalogue (CV-LINT-HOTPATH, BENCH-2)
body:
## Context
`xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` is adopted completely (ADR-0016 Accepted) for every catalogue lifecycle B1-B20, but per-tick rule/aggregation evaluation stays plain code: BENCH-2 measured 381 ev/s against the statechart runtime versus the 2,000 ev/s CVD/delta needs (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4d). `CvdEngine` and delta aggregation are explicitly excluded from the catalogue (§3), and this Chore makes that exclusion a checked invariant instead of a comment.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `CV-LINT-HOTPATH` fixture (extending the `tools/lint_statecharts.py` AST lint owned by `E50-T11`) that fails CI if `CvdEngine`, delta-aggregation modules, or any per-trade footprint path imports `xstate_statemachine`, `statechart.factory`, or `statechart.gateway`.
- A short BENCH-2 note added to the ADR-0017 draft (the CVD/footprint architecture ADR) recording the 381 ev/s vs 2,000 ev/s measurement as the permanent reason for the exclusion.

## Out of scope
- Re-running BENCH-2 itself - already measured in the xstate battle research; this Chore only encodes the conclusion as a lint fixture and a doc note.
- Any other hot-path exclusion (order book reconstruction, paper matcher) - those get their own `CV-LINT-HOTPATH` fixture entries under the epics that own them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Lint fails on an accidental statechart import in the hot path
  Given a change adds `from candleviewer.statechart import factory` inside CvdEngine
  When CV-LINT-HOTPATH runs
  Then CI fails with a message naming BENCH-2 as the reason

Scenario: Lint passes on the unmodified engine
  Given CvdEngine and delta aggregation as implemented in E23-T01
  When CV-LINT-HOTPATH runs
  Then it passes
